title: Attribution-based diagnostics for single-cell foundation models
abstract: Single-cell RNA foundation models (scFMs) are increasingly used for in-silico biological discovery, yet predictive performance alone does not reveal whether their decisions rely on biologically meaningful signals or model-specific shortcuts. We systematically investigate post-hoc attribution of downstream predictions across two tasks: cell-type annotation using pretrained Cell2Sentence and scGPT models, and perturbation prediction using scGPT+STATE in a controlled setting. For cell annotation, we use attribution to assess whether predictions rely on established marker genes and how their relevance varies with model architecture, expression rank, and the surrounding cellular context. For perturbation prediction, we compare attribution patterns with known regulatory ground-truth in a synthetic setting to assess what they reveal about the model's learned computations. Across these tasks, attribution reveals biological feature use, contextual interactions, contributions from different input pathways, learning progression, associations with prediction quality, and potential pitfalls that are not fully captured by standard performance metrics. Experiments with complete and limited regulatory knowledge further demonstrate that conclusions drawn from attribution depend strongly on the choice of biological reference, baseline, and null model. Together, these findings highlight the value of attribution as a flexible post-hoc diagnostic for understanding model behavior, identifying potential issues, and informing the development of scFMs.

title: Poly(acrylamido) PEG-Alternative Lipids Rescue mRNA Efficacy during Repeated Dosing and Enhance Immune Cell Delivery.
abstract: Following the successes of the messenger RNA (mRNA) lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccines against COVID-19, mRNA-LNPs are being explored for varied multidose applications including cancer immunotherapies and protein replacement therapies. LNPs rely on poly(ethylene glycol)-lipid (PEG-lipid) coatings for stability, but increasing anti-PEG antibody prevalence threatens repeat-dose efficacy and increases pseudoallergic risk, creating an urgent need for alternatives. Here, we introduce poly(acrylamido) lipids (PAM-lipids), a family of polymer lipids that effectively replace PEG-lipids in mRNA-LNP formulations. Systematic variation of monomer chemistry, molar mass, and end group reveals critical structure-activity relationships determining LNP size, polydispersity, and transfection efficiency. Varying PAM monomer chemistry allows minimization of antipolymer antibody cross-reactivity, with multiple PAM-lipids demonstrating no anti-PEG antibody binding. Several PAM-LNPs exhibit superior mRNA transfection efficacy to PEGylated clinical benchmarks in vitro and in vivo across multiple cell types, organs, routes of administration, and mRNA cargos. In particular, lead PAM-LNPs enhance mRNA delivery to dendritic cells (up to 120-fold in vitro and 3-fold in vivo) and macrophages (4-fold in vivo), with 2.5-fold superior lymph node expression, driven in part by increased cellular association and lymphoid targeting. Crucially, PAM-LNPs evade circulating anti-PEG antibodies to rescue lost mRNA efficacy after repeated dosing, resulting in 300% mRNA expression relative to that of PEG-LNPs. These findings demonstrate PAM-lipids as a chemically varied, immunologically compatible family of PEG alternatives for mRNA-LNP therapeutics.

title: The African swine fever virus I73R protein is a multifunctional Zα domain that mediates both Z-binding-dependent and -independent biological functions through induction of phase separation.
abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) I73R encodes a protein consisting only of a Zalpha (Zα) domain. Here, we studied its biochemical properties. Complementary approaches demonstrated that I73R is a multifunctional Zα domain that combines Z-binding, B-to-Z conversion, and liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) induction activities. I73R proved to be a better converter than human ADAR1 Zα, and it retained conversion activity with Y48I mutation of its Z-binding site. Next, we investigated I73R biological functions, leading to the following findings: (i) Ectopic expression of I73R or mutated I73R with deficient Z-binding both inhibited arsenite-induced stress granules to a similar extent, and none of these proteins localized within these organelles. (ii) I73R formed cytosolic condensates with dsRNA, Z-DNA, and Z-RNA in ASFV-infected cells. (iii) Rescuing of ASFV I73R deletion by sequences encoding natural, mutated, and chimeric forms of Zα domains demonstrated that I73R mediated both Z-binding-dependent and -independent biological functions through induction of LLPS. This conclusion was further supported by the effect of the LLPS inhibitor 1,6-hexanediol on the replication of ASFV I73R recombinant strains. This study further demonstrates the functional diversity that exists among Zα domains. It unravels new outlooks targeting Zα domain-mediated LLPS for the development of pharmaceutical molecules able to regulate viral and cellular Zα domain-containing proteins.

title: In silico design of bivalent multi-epitope mRNA vaccine candidates against Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Chlamydia pneumoniae.
abstract: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) remains a major global health concern. Mycoplasma pneumoniae (M. pneumoniae) and Chlamydia pneumoniae (C. pneumoniae) are important atypical CAP pathogens, and reported coinfection may complicate diagnosis and management. However, no licensed vaccine simultaneously targeting both pathogens is currently available. In this context, mRNA-based multi-epitope vaccines represent a promising platform for bivalent vaccine design because they allow the integration of multiple epitopes into a single construct and may support both humoral and cellular immune responses. This study aimed to design bivalent multi-epitope mRNA vaccine candidates against M. pneumoniae and C. pneumoniae using an immunoinformatics-based strategy. Conserved cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL), helper T-lymphocyte (HTL), and linear B lymphocyte (LBL) epitopes were screened from selected antigenic proteins. Two constructs, MCV1 and MCV2, were assembled with distinct N-terminal immunostimulatory or helper-epitope modules and evaluated for antigenicity, safety, physicochemical and structural properties, receptor docking, three independent 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, replicate-level MM-PBSA, immune simulation, population coverage, human codon optimization, and RNA secondary structure. A total of 11 CTL, 5 HTL, and 14 LBL epitopes with ≥ 90% conservancy among the analyzed strain sequences were selected. Both core constructs were predicted to be antigenic, non-toxic, non-allergenic, and structurally acceptable. HADDOCK refinement yielded cluster-level scores of - 394.3 ± 7.3 for MCV1-TLR2 and - 399.0 ± 5.5 for the exploratory MCV2-TLR4 complex. Across three independent trajectories, MM-PBSA total binding free energies were - 125.19 ± 20.13 and - 126.87 ± 12.73 kcal/mol, respectively. C-ImmSim generated modeled profiles involving humoral and cellular immune components, and the estimated global population coverage was 97.90%. Human codon optimization yielded codon adaptation index values of 0.92 and 0.91 and GC contents of 61.06% and 60.94% for MCV1 and MCV2, respectively. In this in silico study, two bivalent multi-epitope mRNA vaccine candidates against M. pneumoniae and C. pneumoniae were computationally prioritized. These findings provide a theoretical basis for subsequent experimental validation, while in vitro and in vivo studies are still required to verify their actual immunogenicity, protective efficacy, and safety.

title: Adverse effects of FDA-approved RNA therapeutics: a cross-platform analysis of RNA design, delivery systems, and safety profiles.
abstract: RNA therapeutics have emerged as a promising and effective tool to treat a wide range of genetic, metabolic, infectious, and neurodegenerative diseases by directly modulating the gene expression or directing transient protein production. Currently, more than 20 RNA-based drugs have been approved by the FDA, and due to their recent introduction into the clinical practice, long-term safety data remain limited and comparisons of adverse effects across platforms are lacking. This review focuses on the three major RNA therapeutic platforms, including antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), small interfering RNA (siRNA) and messenger RNA (mRNA) and intends to provide a cross-platform analysis of their adverse effects. We searched studies published up to June 2026 in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar using terms related to RNA therapeutics, individual drug names, safety and toxicity outcomes. Clinical trials, extension studies, pharmacovigilance reports, regulatory documents, and prescribing information were considered for each FDA-approved ASO, siRNA and mRNA agent. The observed safety profiles are associated with an interaction between RNA modality and additional determinants, including chemical modification, delivery system, route of administration, biodistribution, target tissue, and clinical context. Innate immune activation represents a potential shared mechanism, whereas sequence-dependent off-target effects, delivery-associated reactions, administration-related complications, and organ-specific toxicities differ in relevance and mechanism among ASO, siRNA, and mRNA therapeutics. Although most reported adverse effects are mild to moderate, important research gaps regarding long-term safety, pediatric use and rare adverse effects still exist, underscoring the need for further optimization of RNA drug design and delivery technologies, as well as continued pharmacovigilance.

title: Exosome-shuttled PCBP1 from hypoxic preconditioned urine-derived stem cells accelerates wound healing.
abstract: We previously found that hypoxia-preconditioned human urine-derived stem cells (USCs) accelerated wound healing. Since exosomes are one of the key mediator of USCs to support skin repair, we wonder whether the healing-promoting effects of hypoxia-treated USCs were associated with exosomes. A full-thickness cutaneous wound model of female C57BL/6J mice was established. Label-free exosome proteomics was performed to investigate the differentially expression protein from exosomes derived from hypoxia-treated USCs (H-USCs-exo). Transcriptomics was carried out to explore the downstream signaling of exosome recipient cells. H-USCs-exo facilitated the wound healing via angiogenesis and re-epithelialization. Also, the pro-angiogenesis results were obtained in vitro, as evidenced by the enhancement of proliferation, migration, and angiogenic abilities of human microvascular endothelial cell line HMEC-1. Subsequently, using Label-free exosome proteomics, a protein named poly (RC) binding protein 1 (PCBP1, an RNA-binding protein) was found to be significantly upregulated (Fold change = 3.34, p < 0.05) in H-USCs-exo. Exosomes delivered PCBP1 into endothelial cells, and exosomal PCBP1 mediated the pro-angiogenic effects of H-USCs-exo on HMEC-1 cells. The healing-delaying function was confirmed in mice treated with exosomes secreted by hypoxia-pretreated USCs with PCBP1 knockdown. In addition, as a tissue repair facilitator, hypoxia inducible factor 1 subunit alpha (HIF-1α) was upregulated in USCs under hypoxia condition. HIF-1α potentiated the transcription of PCBP1, leading to the high abundance of PCBP1 in H-USCs and H-USCs-exo. Further high-throughput transcriptomics illustrated that PCBP1 upregulated the expression of WNT5A (Fold change = 2.75, p < 0.05) and its downstream factors including vascular endothelial growth factor A and TEK receptor tyrosine kinase (Fold change = 2.85 and 5.75, respectively; p < 0.05). Exosome-shuttled PCBP1 from hypoxic preconditioned USCs accelerated wound healing, which might be associated with WNT5A signaling pathway.

title: Coacervate droplets as a liquefier for the solid-to-liquid transition of RNA aggregates.
abstract: Biomolecular condensates are functionally gated by their material properties. While RNA is a primary structural scaffold, its sequence-specific interactions can aberrantly drive condensates into dysfunctional solid aggregates. Yet, actively reversing this solidification to restore function remains a fundamental challenge, impeding progress in synthetic biology and therapeutics interventions. Here, we establish that complex coacervates can be engineered as liquefiers to actively remodel solid RNA-peptide aggregates into functional liquid droplets. Integrating systematic experiments with all-atom simulations, we decode a multiscale mechanism: coacervate infiltration at the micrometer scale mediates molecular buffering at the nanometer scale, which fluidizes the crosslinked network to drive macroscopic liquefaction. This capability is governed by a design rule, where coacervates formed by small-molecular anions exhibit optimal efficacy. We deploy this principle to functionally rescue silenced RNA within a model of pathologically solidified ribonucleoprotein assemblies. Our work provides a general framework for the active, compositional control of biomolecular phase behavior, with direct implications for managing pathological aggregation and engineering functional condensates in synthetic and living systems.
extra: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

title: Hypothalamic lncRNA Synage prevents age-related sperm quality decline by suppressing A-type potassium currents in GnRH neurons.
abstract: Age-related decline in male fertility, including diminished sperm quality, poses significant risks to offspring health and is exacerbated by modern trends toward delayed parenthood. Focusing on the hypothalamus-pituitary-testis axis, which governs hormonal control of male reproduction, we identified Synage, a long noncoding RNA expressed in the hypothalamic medial preoptic area (mPOA). We found that Synage expression in gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons decreases with age, correlating with reduced sperm quality and male fertility. mPOA-targeted Synage_B (brain-specific isoform) supplementation increases serum testosterone and improves sperm count and progressive motility in 12-mo-old mice. Conversely, conditional deletion of Synage in GnRH neurons in young mice reduces GnRH neuron firing, decreases serum LH and testosterone levels, impaires sperm quality, and reduces male fertility. Mechanistically, Synage interacts with the heat shock protein HSPA8 and stabilizes the HSPA8-KCHIP4 interaction. Synage loss increases KCHIP4 abundance and its association with the Kv4.2 channel, promoting Kv4.2 membrane recruitment and enhancing A-type potassium currents (IA), thereby reducing GnRH neuronal excitability. Consistent with this model, GnRH neurons from 12-mo-old mice also exhibit reduced excitability. Together, these findings support a role for age-dependent Synage loss in reproductive decline, at least in part through dysregulation of the HSPA8-KCHIP4-Kv4.2 pathway and reduced GnRH neuron excitability. These findings identify Synage as a candidate regulator of reproductive aging and motivate further investigation of its translational potential.
extra: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

title: In vitro antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antifungal, and anti-HCoV-229E activities of Jatropha integerrima leaf and stem bark extract and in vivo evaluation of its intravenous SNEDDS in a mouse model.
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has highlighted the need for novel antiviral agents with additional therapeutic activities against inflammatory and opportunistic fungal infections, including mucormycosis. To evaluate the in vitro antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antifungal, and antiviral activities of ethanolic leaf and stem bark extract of Jatropha integerrima (JIJ) and its in vivo efficacy against Human Coronavirus 229E (HCoV-229E). Antioxidant activity was assessed using DPPH and ABTS assays. Anti-inflammatory activity was evaluated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated THP-1 monocytes and RAW 264.7 macrophages by analysing TNF-α and iNOS gene expression. Antifungal activity was investigated against Apophysomyces elegans and Rhizopus oryzae. Cytotoxicity and antiviral activity were assessed in A549 cells. Optimized JIJ-containing self-nanoemulsifying drug delivery system (JIJ-SNEDDS) was evaluated in BALB/c mice intranasally infected with HCoV-229E. JIJ exhibited strong antioxidant activity, downregulated TNF-α and iNOS expression, and demonstrated antifungal activity against both fungal pathogens. The extract inhibited viral replication in A549 cells with minimal cytotoxicity. Optimized JIJ-SNEDDS exhibited a particle size of 115 ± 1.4 nm and zeta potential of - 32.7 ± 2.1 mV. In infected mice, treatment markedly reduced lung viral load and histopathological damage. RT-PCR and protein analyses confirmed decreased viral RNA and protein levels. Flow cytometry revealed an increased Th1/Th2 ratio, decreased Th17/Treg ratio, and increased B- and natural killer (NK)-cell populations. Serum interleukin-6 (IL-6) and TNF-α levels were also reduced. JIJ-SNEDDS demonstrated promising preclinical antiviral activity against HCoV-229E, accompanied by immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory effects. These findings warrant further investigation of its therapeutic potential against coronavirus infection and associated inflammatory complications.

title: An alfalfa MYB71-centered activation-attenuation module fine-tunes redox homeostasis and drought tolerance in Medicago sativa.
abstract: Drought severely constrains alfalfa (Medicago sativa L.) productivity, yet dissecting drought-response mechanisms in this important perennial forage crop remains challenging because of its highly heterozygous autotetraploid genome, the extended cycle required for stable transformation and regeneration, and the time-consuming evaluation of drought responses in mature plants. Here, we identified MsMYB71, a drought-responsive R2R3-MYB transcription factor, as a positive regulator of drought tolerance in alfalfa. Mechanistically, MsMYB71 directly bound to the promoter of MsPrxQ (peroxiredoxin Q), encoding a chloroplast-associated peroxiredoxin Q, and activated its expression, thereby promoting redox homeostasis under drought stress. In contrast, MsPRL1 (PLEIOTROPIC REGULATORY LOCUS 1, a WD40-repeat protein) and MsCUL4 (Cullin4, a Cullin-family scaffold protein) interacted with MsMYB71 and attenuated its protein accumulation and transcriptional output. To establish the physiological relevance of this regulatory module directly in alfalfa, we generated stable overexpression and RNA interference lines for all four genes. Genetic and physiological analyses showed that MsMYB71 enhanced drought tolerance and restricted excessive reactive oxygen species accumulation. Stable manipulation of MsPrxQ further established its positive role in drought tolerance and antioxidant defense. In contrast, MsPRL1 and MsCUL4 negatively regulated drought tolerance and physically interacted with MsMYB71. Their co-expression reduced MsMYB71 protein accumulation in a proteasome-sensitive manner and attenuated MsMYB71-dependent activation of MsPrxQ, consistent with an MsPRL1/MsCUL4-associated attenuation mechanism. Together, our findings define an MsPRL1/MsCUL4-MsMYB71-MsPrxQ module that couples transcriptional activation with protein-level attenuation to fine-tune redox homeostasis and drought adaptation in alfalfa.

title: HIV-1 Vpr: a multifunctional accessory protein with potential contributions to AIDS pathogenesis and persistence.
abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection can progress to acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS), which is characterized by a rapid decline in CD4+ T lymphocyte counts, severe impairment of host immune competence, and recurrent opportunistic infections. Over the past four decades, HIV infection has remained one of the major threats to global public health. Viral protein R (Vpr) is one of nine proteins encoded by HIV RNA genome. Despite consisting of merely 96 amino acids, Vpr exerts multiple functions throughout viral infection and replication and is potentially associated with the progression of AIDS. In this review, we summarize the structural features and biological functions of Vpr, and focus on its multifaceted roles, including the induction of G2/M cell-cycle arrest and apoptotic cell death, facilitation of HIV-1 infection and replication via Env enhancement, modulation of cellular signaling cascades and host gene expression, and participation in AIDS progression. We also include Vpr-mediated regulation of human endogenous retroelement activity and its potential impacts on cellular innate immune responses. This work aims to provide novel analytical perspectives and research directions for in-depth elucidation of Vpr functions and their contributions to AIDS pathogenesis.

title: Majorbio Cloud 2026 provides comprehensive analysis workflows for microbiome.
abstract: The integrated microbiome data analysis platform on Majorbio Cloud (https://cloud.majorbio.com/) encompasses 26 analytical workflows, with a core architecture of two modules: single-omics workflows and cross-omics integration and correlation workflows. The platform supports multi-scale microbiome research (strain to community levels) and cross-omics analyses spanning DNA, RNA, protein, and metabolite layers. The platform features four key functions: (1) Application guide, streamlines analytical workflows for user convenience; (2) Default analysis parameters and one-click analysis, enables one-step data processing; (3) One-click plot enhancement, optimizes figures to meet academic publication standards; (4) Plot patchwork feature, stores optimized images in my gallery, facilitates the creation of publication-ready image composites, supports composite downloads in PDF/PNG/SVG formats, and allows the preservation of patchwork templates for subsequent applications. By late 2025, the platform has facilitated over 5,050 scientific publications, accelerating microbiome research advances.

title: Association of Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C Virus Infections With Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review of Virological, Histopathological, and Molecular Evidence.
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are major but biologically distinct causes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This systematic review synthesized virological, histopathological, genomic, and molecular evidence linking HBV and HCV infections with HCC and compared their dominant pathways of hepatocarcinogenesis. The review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception through June 30, 2026, supplemented by backward citation searching. Human primary studies evaluating HBV- or HCV-associated HCC using virological, histopathological, genomic, epigenetic, or molecular outcomes were eligible. Of 310 records identified, 278 were screened after duplicate removal, 60 full-text reports were assessed, and 25 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Meta-analysis was not undertaken because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Prospective HBV studies demonstrated strong virological risk gradients. Combined hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis B e antigen positivity was associated with an adjusted relative risk of 60.2 (95% confidence interval: 35.5-102.1) for HCC, while HCC incidence increased from 108 to 1,152 per 100,000 person-years across increasing HBV DNA categories. Molecular studies consistently demonstrated enrichment of HBV DNA integration in tumor tissue, with recurrent involvement of telomerase reverse transcriptase and other cancer-associated loci, together with insertional mutagenesis and structural genomic alterations. In HCV infection, cumulative HCC risk increased from 1.1% among HCV RNA-negative individuals to 6.4% and 14.7% among low- and high-viremia groups, respectively. HCV-associated HCC was more closely linked to chronic necroinflammation, oxidative injury, fibrosis, cirrhosis, viral protein-mediated signaling, and persistent epigenetic alterations rather than viral genome integration. Histopathological evidence generally demonstrated greater background necroinflammation and cirrhosis in HCV-associated HCC, whereas HBV-associated HCC could occur in less fibrotic or noncirrhotic liver. HBV and HCV therefore converge on hepatocarcinogenesis through chronic liver injury but differ in their dominant mechanisms. HBV has a prominent direct oncogenic component involving viral DNA integration and genomic instability, whereas HCV-associated HCC is predominantly driven by inflammation-, fibrosis-, and cirrhosis-associated carcinogenesis with additional molecular and epigenetic effects. Viral suppression or eradication reduces but does not completely eliminate HCC risk after advanced hepatic or persistent molecular injury has developed.

title: Express delivery: dsRNA applications and RNAi nanocarrier systems to combat potato late blight.
abstract: Phytophthora late blight remains one of the most devastating diseases of potatoes, posing persistent challenges to global food security and sustainable agriculture. Although RNA interference (RNAi) has emerged as a powerful and highly specific strategy for pathogen control, its practical application against P. infestans has largely remained at the proof-of-concept stage. This limitation does not result from a lack of suitable gene targets, but rather from challenges associated with the delivery, stability, and uptake of RNA molecules under field conditions. In this review, we outline current advances in RNAi-based approaches for the control of P. infestans, with a particular focus on spray-induced gene silencing (SIGS) and the potential of nanocarrier-based delivery systems. We summarize proof-of-concept studies targeting essential oomycete genes, discuss the molecular mechanisms underlying double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) uptake in plants and oomycetes, and critically evaluate the strengths and limitations of host-induced gene silencing (HIGS) and SIGS. Unlike recent reviews on nanocarrier-mediated RNA delivery, this manuscript provides a system-specific focus centered on the potato-P. infestans pathosystem and the unique biological features of the plant-oomycete interface. Central to this review is the argument that future success of RNAi-based disease management will require systems‑level optimization that integrates target selection, dsRNA design, formulation, delivery, and application timing, while emphasizing that delivery remains a major bottleneck for translation to field applications. We highlight how nanocarriers can enhance dsRNA stability, improve adhesion and cellular uptake, and enable controlled release, thereby transforming SIGS into a robust and environmentally sustainable plant protection strategy. Finally, we position RNAi-based nanobiopesticides within the broader European regulatory and sustainability landscape, emphasizing both regulatory feasibility and the importance of public trust and societal acceptance. Together, these insights position nanocarrier-enabled SIGS as a promising cornerstone of next-generation, sustainable late blight management.

title: Nano differential scanning fluorimetry in drug discovery: advances, applications, and limitations.
abstract: Nano differential scanning fluorimetry monitors changes in the intrinsic tryptophan and tyrosine fluorescence of a target protein during thermal unfolding, providing a label-free approach to assessing protein stability and ligand engagement in early-stage drug discovery. The authors examine the technical differences between nano differential scanning fluorimetry and dye-based differential scanning fluorimetry, including sample demand, throughput, buffer and solvent compatibility, and optical artifacts. In addition, the authors present applications in fragment screening, hit validation, and the characterization of oligomeric, allosteric, membrane, proximity-induced degradation modalities and RNA-binding targets. Finally, the limitations arising from reporter distribution, noncooperative unfolding, aggregation, and complex matrices are highlighted. This review is based on literature searches using PubMed and Google Scholar to identify articles published between 2001 and 2026. NanoDSF is most valuable as a context-dependent primary or orthogonal method rather than a universal high-throughput replacement. Its future impact will depend on automation, analysis of raw fluorescence and scattering, validated reconstituted systems, and integration with quantitative binding, structural, and functional assays. Expansion to cell-like matrices will require target-specific deconvolution.

title: De Novo transcriptome assembly and functional annotation in non-model organisms.
abstract: Advances in RNA sequencing have established transcriptomics as a key approach for investigating gene expression, regulation, and functional diversity across both model and non-model organisms. In the absence of high-quality reference genomes, de novo transcriptome assembly remains essential, yet its accuracy and reproducibility depend heavily on the choice and integration of computational strategies. This review provides a comprehensive and structured framework for de novo transcriptome reconstruction and functional annotation in non-model systems, integrating current best practices across quality control, assembly, redundancy reduction, and annotation workflows. We systematically compare short-read, long-read, and hybrid assembly approaches, and evaluate multi-layered annotation strategies combining homology-based, domain-based, and ontology-driven methods. We further highlight emerging developments, including long-read transcriptomics, machine learning-assisted annotation, orthology inference, and multi-omics integration, which improve transcriptome completeness and biological interpretability. Key limitations in current workflows are critically examined, including database biases, incomplete annotations, and challenges in isoform resolution, particularly in underrepresented taxa. By consolidating methodological advances with practical recommendations, this review proposes a reproducible and scalable roadmap for transcriptome analysis in non-model organisms. We also discuss future directions, including the development of inclusive reference databases, AI-driven annotation frameworks, and open, containerized infrastructures aligned with FAIR principles to support global transcriptomics research.

title: Selective profiling of translationally active tRNAs and their dynamics under stress.
abstract: During translation, transfer RNAs (tRNAs) deliver specific amino acids to the ribosome in a coordinated manner with the sequence encoded by the messenger RNA. Despite their central role in protein synthesis, their precise contribution to the modulation of translation remains poorly understood, primarily due to lack of methods to characterize tRNA abundances and their modifications from actively translating ribosomes. Here we develop tRIBO-seq, a simple and robust nanopore-based method to selectively capture ribosome-associated native tRNA populations (ribo-tRNAs) from actively translating ribosomes, providing tRNA abundance, modification and fragmentation information from a single experiment. Using tRIBO-seq, we find that ribo-tRNAs, but often not total tRNAs, are significantly altered on stress. Notably, we find that tRNAome alterations strongly vary depending on the stress type; while viral infection and leucine deprivation leads to changes in ribo-tRNA abundances, methionine starvation causes a dramatic loss of methyl-based tRNA modifications. By contrast, we find that arsenite exposure does not alter tRNA abundances nor modification patterns, but rather causes major fragmentation events in selected subsets of ribo-tRNAs. Altogether, tRIBO-seq offers a robust and reproducible approach to map the full tRNA landscape-capturing tRNA abundance, modification and fragmentation patterns-across both total and actively translating tRNA populations, revealing the dynamics of the tRNAome with unprecedented resolution, in a single experiment.

title: Characterization of peritrophin-like protein PvPT-L1 from Penaeus Vannamei: Potential association with dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase DLD from Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Ep-M17 and implications for probiotic adhesion and immune modulation.
abstract: Probiotics are widely used to promote growth and health in Penaeus vannamei; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying their interaction with the host remain poorly understood. In this study, we identified a peritrophin-like factor, PvPT-L1, as a putative critical mediator of the probiotic effects of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Ep-M17. Full-length cloning revealed that PvPT-L1 contains three typical chitin-binding domains and shares high homology with Penaeus japonicus PT-L1. PvPT-L1 was predominantly expressed in the midgut, with considerable transcript abundance in the hepatopancreas and foregut. In vitro binding assays confirmed that recombinant rPvPT-L1 may bind to chitin and associated with both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Notably, PvPT-L1 significantly enhanced the intestinal adherence of L. plantarum Ep-M17 in a HEK-293 T cell model. RNA interference (RNAi) against PvPT-L1 resulted in 466 differentially expressed genes, disrupting redox homeostasis, proteostasis, and transmembrane transport, suggesting its essential role in maintaining gut barrier integrity. Using His pull-down and LC-MS/MS, we identified dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase (DLD) that may be associated with bacterial cells as a potential interacting partner of PvPT-L1; this interaction was further validated by molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and co-immunoprecipitation. Functionally, oral administration of recombinant rDLD appeared to mitigated intestinal epithelial apoptosis. Interestingly, although rDLD suppressed hemocyte phagocytic activity, it effectively reprogrammed immune effector transcription and alleviated pathogen-induced apoptosis, hinting at a shift from robust internalization toward balanced immunomodulation. Collectively, these findings provide insights into a potential DLD-PvPT-L1 axis that may link physical adhesion and immune calibration, offering new mechanistic clues into probiotic-host immune interactions in crustaceans.

title: Replacing corn-silage in total mixed rations for fattening bulls with dry components: effects on rumen health, the buccal and faecal microbiome and the plasma metabolome.
abstract: The exchange of feed components in a diet requires a concise ration adjustment to obtain a ration that is rumen-safe, as well as energy- and protein-balanced. The growth rates achievable with a straw- and concentrate-based ration, supplemented with by-products (DRY), were previously shown to equal those obtained with an isocaloric and isonitrogenous conventional corn silage-based ration (CONVL) throughout a 9-month fattening period in 24 Simmental bulls. Differences in fibre composition and particle size may nevertheless affect gut health and result in subclinical alterations. We therefore investigated rumen health, the buccal and faecal microbiota using 16S ribosomal RNA gene sequencing, and the plasma metabolome. Bulls fed the DRY diet showed decreased rumen motility and increased rumen wall thickness, indicating long-term effects on the rumen. The plasma metabolomic profiles from 51 and 63 weeks of age (28 and 40 weeks on feed) exhibited specific alterations in the DRY-fed bulls, with increased levels of trimethylamine N-oxide and methionine sulfoxide, and decreased levels of hippuric acid and 3-indolepropionic acid, suggesting potential oxidative and metabolic stress. In addition, lipid metabolism was altered in DRY-fed bulls, with changes in phosphatidylcholines, cholesterol esters, and triglycerides. Buccal swab samples collected at week 63 of age showed lower alpha diversity and fewer amplicon sequence variants in DRY-fed than in CONVL-fed bulls, whereas faecal alpha diversity did not differ between diets. Beta-diversity ordination showed more pronounced diet-associated separation in buccal swab samples than in faecal samples. Differential abundance analysis showed less butyrate-producing Butyrivibrio, Pseudobutyrivibrio and Lachnospiraceae, as well as intestinal mucosa-maintaining Akkermansia, in the DRY-fed bulls than in the CONVL group, following the differences in the intake of physically effective NDF. These findings suggest that while both total mixed rations supported similar growth performance, the DRY diet affected rumen and metabolic health and altered the microbial composition, indicating that the animals' capacity to adapt to certain diets might reach its limits.

title: Persistent Circulating Proteomic Signatures Distinguish Magnetic Resonance Angiography-Defined Carotid Plaque Vulnerability.
abstract: Carotid artery luminal stenosis alone may not predict the risk of future neurovascular events. Plaque vulnerability is emerging as an independent predictor of higher risk for a neurovascular event. We evaluated blood proteomics, paired with high-resolution cross-sectional imaging preoperatively. From preoperative and postoperative blood samples, our objective was to identify blood proteins that distinguish patients with vulnerable and non-vulnerable carotid artery plaques. We conducted an exploratory, single-center proteomic study of 27 consecutive patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy with preoperative 3.0T magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging. Plaques were classified as vulnerable when magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging identified at least one high-risk feature: thin fibrous cap, lipid-rich necrotic core, ulceration, intraplaque hemorrhage, or inflammation. Serum samples were analyzed preoperatively and postoperatively using a high-throughput, untargeted proteomics technology (Olink). Differential protein abundance between vulnerable and non-vulnerable groups was assessed separately at each time point. For both time points, the vulnerable group demonstrated a blood proteomic signature involving diacylglycerol signaling and oxidative stress proteins, including diacylglycerol kinase iota and peroxiredoxin-like 2B, with postoperative vulnerability additionally associated with platelet activation (Ras guanyl releasing protein 2), cytoskeletal remodeling (metastasis suppressor 1), and ribonucleic acid/ribosome-related proteins (Shwachman-Bodian-Diamond syndrome protein, RNA-binding protein with multiple splicing 2, zinc ribbon domain-containing protein 2). Non-vulnerable plaques showed a higher abundance of proteins involved in cellular maintenance and deoxyribonucleic acid repair. Furthermore, the persistence of higher diacylglycerol kinase iota and peroxiredoxin-like 2B in the vulnerable group and X-ray repair cross-complementing protein 2 in the non-vulnerable group at both time points suggests stable, patient-level systemic differences detectable in blood, despite plaque removal. Serum proteomics identified distinct systemic pathways associated with cross-sectional imaging carotid plaque vulnerability, highlighting diacylglycerol signaling, oxidative stress, and platelet activation as candidate mechanisms and new biomarker candidates for risk stratification, symptom surveillance, and targeted medical interventions.

title: Inclisiran attenuates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury by inhibiting macrophage M1 polarization.
abstract: Macrophage polarization is pivotal in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. Inclisiran is a small interfering RNA agent that lowers low-density lipoprotein cholesterol by targeting proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9). However, whether Inclisiran exerts LDL-C-independent cardioprotective effects within the acute I/R window remains unclear. In this study, wild-type C57BL/6J mice were pretreated with Inclisiran before I/R surgery. Myocardial injury was assessed by echocardiography, laser speckle contrast imaging, and TTC/Evans Blue staining. Macrophage polarization and its direct impact on cardiomyocytes or fibroblasts were investigated in co-culture system in vitro. Target gene screening was performed by chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-sequencing, and transcriptional regulation was validated by dual-luciferase assay and ChIP-qPCR. Protein interaction was confirmed by molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance, and co-immunoprecipitation. Our results demonstrated that Inclisiran significantly attenuated myocardial injury and dysfunction, inhibited macrophage M1 polarization, reduced cardiomyocyte apoptosis, and suppressed fibroblast activation. Mechanistically, Inclisiran disrupted the direct interaction between PCSK9 and JNK, thereby blocking the HIF-1α-mediated transcriptional regulation of Myo1d, and ultimately suppressing macrophage M1 polarization. In conclusion, Inclisiran alleviates myocardial I/R injury by targeting the JNK-HIF-1α-Myo1d signaling axis. These findings identify a previously unrecognized cardioprotective mechanism that is LDL-C-independent within the acute I/R window, suggesting Inclisiran as a promising therapeutic strategy for ischemic cardiomyopathy.

title: Pectolinarigenin suppresses colorectal cancer progression through metabolism-associated signaling.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden, with metabolic alterations contributing to its malignant behavior. Pectolinarigenin (PEC), a naturally occurring flavonoid, exhibits antitumor activity in several cancers, but its metabolism-associated effects in CRC remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to investigate the anticancer activity of PEC and its effects on glycolysis-associated metabolism and AMPK/FOXO3a-related signaling in CRC. PEC targets were predicted using PharmMapper and SwissTargetPrediction and intersected with CRC-related differentially expressed genes. Functional enrichment analysis, protein-protein interaction analysis, LASSO regression, and single-cell RNA sequencing were integrated to identify candidate genes associated with PEC activity. The effects of PEC were evaluated in HT29 and MC38 cells using proliferation, colony formation, invasion, apoptosis, qRT-PCR, and western blotting assays. AMPK/FOXO3a-related signaling changes were examined in both CRC cell models and MC38 tumor tissues, with selected molecular alterations further assessed by immunohistochemistry in MC38 syngeneic tumors. PEC suppressed CRC cell proliferation, colony formation, and invasion and promoted apoptosis. PEC treatment reduced the expression of the glycolysis-associated molecules GLUT1, HK2, and LDHA, accompanied by increased AMPK phosphorylation and reduced inhibitory FOXO3a phosphorylation in CRC cells. Integrated bioinformatic analyses identified CA1 and CA7 as candidate genes associated with PEC activity, with both genes predominantly localized to epithelial cell populations in single-cell datasets. PEC increased CA1 and CA7 expression in CRC cells and MC38 tumor tissues. Western blotting of tumor tissues further showed increased p-AMPK and reduced p-FOXO3a levels following PEC treatment, consistent with the corresponding changes observed in CRC cells. Immunohistochemical analysis further confirmed increased p-AMPK, CA1, and CA7 staining and reduced p-FOXO3a staining in PEC-treated tumor tissues. PEC exhibits antitumor activity against CRC and is associated with coordinated changes in glycolysis-associated molecules and AMPK/FOXO3a-related signaling. CA1 and CA7 emerged from integrated bioinformatic analyses as metabolism-associated candidate genes and showed consistent expression changes following PEC treatment in CRC cells and tumor tissues. These findings provide a basis for further investigation of the molecular and metabolic responses associated with PEC in CRC.

title: Duration-dependent hippocampal GLUT4 upregulation mediates depressive and cognitive deficits in rats with propylthiouracil-induced hypothyroidism.
abstract: Adult-onset hypothyroidism can cause emotional and memory impairment. However, the underlying mechanism remainsunclear. This study aimed to investigate the effect of short-term hypothyroidism on the expression of GLUT4 in the hippocampus of adultrats and to elucidate the bridging role of abnormal GLUT4 in key brain regions and to explore its potential role in mood and cognitiveimpairment in hypothyroidism. Thirty male Wistar rats were divided into a control group (n = 10), propylthiouracil (PTU)-induced hypothyroid groups (PTU6W/10W/14W, n = 5 each), and PTU14W + levothyroxine (LT4, n = 5). Behavioral tests (open field, novel object recognition,Morris water maze) assessed emotional and cognitive functions. Serum thyroid hormones, glucose, insulin, and hippocampal GLUT4expression [Western blot, quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), immunohistochemistry] were analyzed. Hypothyroid rats exhibited reduced body weight, serum triiodothyronine (T3), thyroxine (T4), glucose, and insulin (p < 0.05), with elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH). Behavioral deficits emerged progressively: PTU6W showed depressive-like behaviors(50% decrease in open field locomotion); PTU10W/14W displayed impaired novel object recognition (30% lower discrimination index);PTU14W had prolonged water maze latency (2-fold increase) and 40% shorter platform quadrant duration. Hippocampal GLUT4 proteinincreased time-dependently (1.8-fold in PTU14W vs. control, p < 0.05), while GLUT4 messenger RNA (mRNA) remained unchanged.Levothyroxine reversed these effects. Short-term hypothyroidism induces depressive-like behaviors, whereas prolonged deficiency exacerbates spatial memory deficits. Compensatory GLUT4 protein upregulation, potentially mediated by insulin signaling, may sustain glucose metabolism duringearly hypothyroidism. However, chronic impairment overwhelms this adaptation, triggering cognitive decline. Dynamic GLUT4 regulation plays a pivotal role in hypothyroidism-related cognitive dysfunction.

title: Integrative Analysis of Epidermal Barrier Dysfunction Regulators in Psoriasis.
abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by keratinocyte hyperproliferation and compromised epidermal barrier function. Although tight junction disruption is a key pathological hallmark, the upstream transcriptional mechanisms driving the downregulation of core barrier proteins such as claudin-1 (CLDN1) remain insufficiently characterized. We implemented an integrative multi-omics framework combining weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and machine-learning algorithms to prioritize core diagnostic features in psoriasis. Upstream transcription factors regulating CLDN1 were computationally predicted using the JASPAR, hTFtarget, and KnockTF databases. The regulatory effect of E74-like ETS transcription factor 3 (ELF3) on the CLDN1 promoter was evaluated using dual-luciferase reporter assays, and the inflammatory response of the axis was examined in TNF-α-stimulated HaCaT keratinocytes via quantitative real-time PCR. Machine-learning prioritization identified CLDN1 as a robust diagnostic feature that is significantly downregulated in psoriatic lesions. Multi-database integration converged on ELF3 as a candidate negative regulator of CLDN1. Dual-luciferase reporter assays demonstrated that ELF3 overexpression significantly suppressed wild-type CLDN1 promoter activity, whereas mutation of the predicted binding site abolished this repression. In TNF-α-stimulated HaCaT cells, ELF3 was markedly upregulated with a concurrent downregulation of CLDN1. These findings suggest that ELF3 functions as a candidate transcriptional repressor of CLDN1 promoter activity and provide preliminary in vitro and computational insights into the transcriptional alterations associated with epidermal barrier disruption in psoriasis, highlighting potential avenues for restoring structural barrier integrity.

title: Preharvest soybean meal supplementation alters tissue-specific protein and amino acid composition in Morchella sextelata: integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analysis.
abstract: Preharvest nutrient inputs can modify mushroom composition, but whether graded supplementation differentially affects the protein and amino acid composition of anatomically distinct fruiting-body tissues remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize the compositional and molecular responses of the cap and stipe of Morchella sextelata to additional soybean meal. Protein and 18 hydrolyzed amino acids were quantified following 0-10% supplementation, while the control, 2%, 4%, and 8% treatments were analyzed by transcriptomics and proteomics. Protein content responded nonlinearly and was highest at 8% in both tissues; total and essential amino acid contents were also highest in 8% caps. However, cap protein-normalized essential amino acid proportionality did not improve correspondingly, distinguishing compositional enrichment from amino acid balance. Caps generally exhibited more differentially expressed genes, whereas stipes contained more differentially expressed proteins, with downregulated proteins predominating in the 2 and 8% stipe comparisons. Integrated analyses associated these responses with carbon and amino acid metabolism, translation, protein homeostasis, energy metabolism, and RNA processing. These findings demonstrate tissue- and molecular-layer-dependent responses to preharvest nutrient supplementation. Future studies should determine whether the associated pathways translate into altered enzyme activities, metabolic fluxes, and sensory-relevant metabolites.

title: Regulation of gene expression in renal papilla and cardiac ventricle in response to dietary Na+ restriction.
abstract: The kidneys and cardiovascular system maintain volume homeostasis and blood pressure by responding to reduction in dietary Na+ intake. We examined Na+-dependent changes in gene expression in the renal papilla and heart ventricle of rats. Animals were conditioned with control or low-Na+ diets for 1 week. RNA isolated from kidneys or hearts was analyzed by RNAseq. In the renal papilla, notable genes upregulated in response to low dietary Na+ included α, β and γ subunits of ENaC, α and β subunits of the Na/K-ATPase, and the transcription factor Zbtb16. Increases in mRNA for the ENaC were confirmed using qPCR and were strongly dependent on location within the kidney with papilla > outer medulla > cortex. Differences in ENaC protein expression exhibited a similar dependence on location. The effects of dietary Na+ on ENaC expression, as well as that of Zbtb16, in the papillae were not mimicked by treatment with aldosterone, indicating that other factors contribute to the adaptation to Na+ deprivation. In the heart, a smaller number of genes were affected by dietary Na+. Effects included downregulation of transcripts for the natriuretic peptides ANP and BNP and of Acta1. Enrichment analyses indicated that low dietary Na+ led to upregulation of many Gene Ontology (GO) gene sets related to growth and development in the kidney samples, but downregulation of such gene sets in the heart. Our results illustrate the profound site- and tissue-specific effects of changes in dietary Na+ on renal and cardiac gene expression and regulation of salt balance.

title: Nucleic Acid Therapeutics in Rare Disease: From Precision Medicine to Programmable Platforms.
abstract: Nucleic acid therapeutics (NATs), including antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics and programmable editing technologies, are reshaping the therapeutic landscape for inherited metabolic and genetic disease. Unlike conventional small molecules or biologics, NATs enable sequence-directed modulation of target gene expression and therefore provide unprecedented flexibility for targeting pathogenic mechanisms previously considered undruggable. Recent clinical successes have established proof of concept for multiple NAT modalities across neurological, hepatic, muscular and metabolic disorders. However, broader implementation remains constrained by challenges in tissue-specific delivery, biomarker validation, natural-history infrastructure and evidence generation in ultra-rare populations. In parallel, increasing platform reproducibility is beginning to challenge traditional product-based regulatory paradigms. This review examines the principal classes of NATs and proposes a practical framework for modality selection based on disease biology, tissue accessibility, durability, reversibility and clinical context. We discuss key translational bottlenecks beyond delivery, including biomarker-outcome relationships, small-population trial design and the limitations of conventional evidentiary frameworks in rare disease. A central theme of this review is the growing transition from isolated precision medicines towards increasingly programmable therapeutic platforms. We explore how advances in extrahepatic delivery, computational oligonucleotide design, artificial intelligence-assisted optimisation and programmable editing technologies may progressively support more scalable and individualised therapeutic development. Finally, we discuss emerging regulatory frameworks that may better accommodate platform-level predictability while maintaining rigorous evaluation of sequence-specific and disease-specific risks.

title: PAR4 exacerbates intracerebral hemorrhage by driving m6A-dependent microglial AIM2 release and neuronal PANoptosis.
abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a neurological disorder with high morbidity and mortality. PAR4 has been implicated in ICH and neuroinflammation. The rat model of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) was established by injecting collagenase into the brain. TTC staining, H&E staining, and immunofluorescence were used to evaluate the brain tissue. In vitro, rat primary microglia (RPMCs) were isolated and the rat microglial cell line HAPI and the hippocampal neuronal cell line H19-7 were cultured. RNA-seq analysis, Western blot, co-immunoprecipitation, cell immunofluorescence, RIP assay, m6A Dot Blot Analysis were performed to investigate the role of PAR4 and its downstream signaling pathways. In the ICH rat model, treatment with the PAR4 antagonist inhibited neuronal death and reversed the M1-dominant shift of microglia. PAR4 regulated m6A methylation in microglia via KIAA1429-mediated recruitment of methyltransferase complexes. PAR4AP increased JAK2 mRNA m6A modification, mRNA and protein levels, and enhanced STAT3 protein phosphorylation. It also increased the expression of inflammatory factors and inflammasome components, with a stronger effect on AIM2 expression. PAR4AP enhanced AIM2 expression in microglial cells through mechanisms dependent on the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway and m6A modification. PAR4AP-activated microglia induce neuronal PANoptosis via exosome-mediated transfer of AIM2, promoting Pyrin-ZBP1 complex formation. In a rat model of ICH, lentivirus-delivered shRNAs targeting KIAA1429, FMR1, and AIM2, as well as PAR4 inhibition, suppressed PANoptosis in neuronal cells. This study provides insights into the role of PAR4 in ICH and its downstream signaling pathways, suggesting potential therapeutic targets for ICH treatment.

title: Yy1 gene function in the bladder epithelium is essential for lower urinary tract morphogenesis.
abstract: Urinary tract morphogenesis is a dynamic process depending on precise coordination between tissues derived from distinct embryonic lineages to establish a functional outflow tract. Disruption of urinary tract development can lead to congenital anomalies, which are among the most common defects diagnosed in neonates. A subset of these malformations arises from impaired distal ureter maturation, a process whereby the ureter separates from the nephric duct and integrates into the bladder wall. Abnormal ureter maturation can cause obstructive uropathies characterized by hydronephrosis and hydroureter. Despite their prevalence and clinical relevance, the molecular mechanisms regulating ureter maturation and obstruction remain poorly understood. Herein, we identify the ubiquitously expressed zinc-finger-containing transcription factor YY1 as an essential regulator of the lower urinary tract development in mice. Conditional inactivation of Yy1 function in the urogenital sinus (UGS), the embryonic bladder-urethra primordium, results in ureteral obstruction, hydronephrosis and hydroureter. Ureters fail to connect with bladder, a defect that correlates with loss of the UGS ridge, a transient structure required for ureter repositioning and maturation, as well as with reduced contractility at the UGS-nephric duct interface. Differentiation of the bladder urothelium is also disrupted, reflecting the YY1 cell-autonomous role in epithelial maturation. Integration of RNA-seq and YY1 chromatin occupancy data reveals that numerous differentially expressed genes are direct YY1 targets, several involved in mitochondrial function and homeostasis. Together, our findings establish YY1 as a key transcriptional regulator of bladder morphogenesis, coordinating ureter-bladder junction formation, promoting urothelial differentiation, and controlling mitochondrial gene networks critical for urinary tract development.

title: CircRNA SNX11 promotes endometrial cell proliferation through GPER1 by sponging hsa-miR-1343-3p.
abstract: Approximately 15% of couples of reproductive age experience infertility. In vitro fertilization (IVF) is the most useful treatment for patients with infertility. However, repeated implantation failure (RIF) is one of the most difficult challenges for the success of IVF, caused by poor endometrial receptivity due to decreased endometrial cell proliferation. This study aimed to investigate the mechanism regulating endometrial cell proliferation to overcome RIF. Hub genes involved in RIF were identified by RNA sequencing for endometrial tissues. The regulatory effects of circular RNA (circRNA) and microRNA (miRNA) in human endometrial stromal cells (hESCs) were determined using miRNA pulldown and dual-luciferase reporter gene assays. Cell proliferation was detected using a Cell Counting Kit-8 assay. G protein-coupled estrogen receptor 1 (GPER1) expression was dramatically downregulated in endometrial tissues obtained from patients with RIF, suggesting that GPER1 might be a hub gene involved in RIF. Additionally, circRNA SNX11 increases GPER1 expression via hsa-miR-1343-3p in hESCs. Additionally, circRNA SNX11 promotes cell proliferation, reduces apoptosis, and modulates RIF-related pathways through GPER1 by sponging hsa-miR-1343-3p in hESCs. This study reveals that circRNA SNX11 facilitates endometrial cell proliferation by upregulating GPER1 by sponging hsa-miR-1343-3p, providing novel therapeutic targets to overcome RIF.

title: Integrative single cell and machine learning analysis identifies fibroblast centric hub genes and therapeutic candidates in lung adenocarcinoma and ischemic cardiomyopathy.
abstract: Ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) are distinct diseases but may share fibroblast mediated mechanisms involving tissue remodeling and inflammation. However, their common molecular features at single cell resolution remain insufficiently defined. We integrated single cell RNA sequencing datasets from ICM and LUAD with bulk transcriptomic profiles from TCGA LUAD, GSE18842, and GSE48166. Differential expression analysis identified 36 shared core genes. A total of 127 combinations of machine learning algorithms and feature selection methods were benchmarked to identify six hub genes: KRTCAP3, RUNX2, DBF4B, C11orf80, COL3A1, and ZFP64. UCell, scMetabolism, SCISSOR, Monocle 3, CellChat, scTenifoldNet/scTenifoldKnk, virtual drug screening, and molecular docking were used for functional characterization. Fibroblasts were the dominant cellular source of the six hub genes in both ICM and LUAD. COL3A1 progressively increased along fibroblast pseudotime trajectories. Virtual overexpression and knockout analyses showed convergence on extracellular matrix organization, inflammatory response, and immune regulation. Cell communication analysis identified fibroblasts as major senders of COLLAGEN signaling, with recipient cells shifting from inflammatory monocytes under normal conditions to proliferating macrophages in ICM and tumor cells in LUAD. Molecular docking nominated Digoxin, Ergotamine, and Ledipasvir as candidate RUNX2-binding compounds with favorable predicted docking scores. This study provides a single cell framework linking ICM and LUAD through fibroblast driven extracellular matrix remodeling and inflammation, and identifies potential molecular targets and therapeutic candidates for further validation.

title: Integrating GWAS, transcriptomics, and machine learning enables genomic prediction of grain cadmium content in malting barley.
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) contamination in arable land poses a serious threat to the production of malting barley, a cornerstone crop for the brewing industry. Excessive Cd in grains undermines malting quality by disrupting germination evenness and reducing enzymatic activity during mashing. Despite this challenge, effective predictive tools for grain Cd levels are scarce, and the genetic architecture controlling this trait remains largely elusive. Here, we employed an integrated strategy combining genome-wide association study (GWAS), RNA-seq, and machine learning across a panel of 100 barley accessions. We benchmarked five genomic prediction algorithms, performed cis-eQTL mapping, and applied multi-omics integration to nominate high-confidence candidate genes. Our GWAS uncovered 3902 Cd-associated SNPs, and the XGBoost model, trained on merely 1000 markers, achieved the highest overall predictive performance (r = 0.86). Through systematic prioritization, we identified 67 candidate metal transporter genes. Among these, HvACA8a emerged as a likely negative modulator of grain Cd loading, whereas HvAHA9 and HvYSL15 were implicated as positive regulators. Collectively, our findings establish a robust genomic prediction framework for early Cd risk evaluation in malting barley. The identified markers and candidate genes offer tangible targets for breeding low-Cd cultivars, thereby helping to safeguard the quality of raw materials destined for the malting and brewing sectors.

title: A Cross-Compartment Five-Gene Host Transcriptomic Signature Distinguishes Active Tuberculosis in Whole Blood and Plasma Cell-free RNA.
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains one of the deadliest infectious diseases worldwide, with gaps in timely, accurate diagnosis sustaining transmission and disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries. Current sputum-based tests show limited sensitivity and poorly distinguish active TB (ATB) from latent infection (LTBI), highlighting the need for reliable non-sputum biomarkers reflecting host disease status. To investigate the conservation of tuberculosis-associated host transcriptomic signals between plasma cell-free RNA and whole blood, and to identify a minimal gene signature for accurate disease classification. We applied an integrated transcriptomic and machine learning framework to discover a biologically plausible minimal gene signature associated with ATB. RNA sequencing data of whole blood, and plasma cell-free RNA available publicly were analysed independently by DESeq2 to determine differentially expressed genes among ATB, LTBI, and healthy controls. Core disease-associated pathways were determined using functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction network analyses. Genes were prioritized based on biological relevance, pathway convergence, and cross-dataset consistency. The resulting gene signature was used to train the machine learning classifiers to evaluate diagnostic performance. Transcriptomic and network analyses revealed that ATB is characterized by interferon-driven immune activation, neutrophil-mediated inflammation, and dysregulated immune regulation, detectable in both whole blood and cfRNA. A five-gene host signature (GBP5, GBP1, ANKRD22, CCR5AS, and KLF2) demonstrated robust diagnostic performance in both whole blood and cfRNA, capturing shared host-response biology despite compartment-specific expression differences. Machine learning models trained on this gene set achieved high diagnostic accuracy, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.98 in whole blood and 0.94 in cfRNA. Notably, CCR5AS, a long non-coding RNA, emerged as a previously underexplored component of host transcriptional responses in TB. A five-gene host-response signature, conserved in whole blood and plasma cfRNA, reliably distinguishes active tuberculosis from latent infection and healthy controls, enabling minimal, cross-platform diagnostics.

title: CDC5L functions as a transcriptional repressor to safeguard against overactive stress response and promote survival.
abstract: Cells have evolved sophisticated molecular and cellular mechanisms to cope with stress. While these stress programs are vital, their overactivation as well as spurious activation in non-stress conditions must be prevented. The mechanisms enforcing this restraint remain unclear. Here, we report that depletion of Cell Division Cycle 5 Like (CDC5L) induces spontaneous stress granule (SG) assembly, and this effect is independent of its established functions in the cell cycle or the PRP19/CDC5L splicing complex. We find that knockdown of CDC5L increases the protein abundance of the stress kinase PERK, and this increase is sufficient to promote eIF2α hyperphosphorylation and trigger SG assembly. Mechanistically, CDC5L binds the PERK promoter via the DNA-binding domains and represses PERK expression. Integrative RNA-seq and ChIP-seq analyses further reveal a dual transcriptional function of CDC5L: it activates the transcription of cell-cycle related genes while repressing that of stress response genes. Consequently, CDC5L depletion leads to widespread upregulation of stress pathways, which elevates stress sensitivity, lowers stress tolerance, and reduces cell and animal survival under stressed conditions. Our findings reveal a crucial role for CDC5L in transcriptional regulation of stress response pathways (e.g., the PERK-eIF2α-SG axis), which may precisely modulate gene expression and coordinate specific cellular programs-such as cell proliferation and stress adaptation-in response to changing conditions.

title: Microfluidic lipid nanoparticles co-delivering siMOB1A and paclitaxel for ovarian cancer therapy.
abstract: Ovarian cancer is the foremost cause of mortality among gynecologic malignancies. Paclitaxel (PTX) exerts a significant therapeutic effect on ovarian cancer by targeting microtubules and impeding the cell cycle progression during the mitosis phase. MOB kinase activator 1 A (MOB1A) has been proven to regulate the cycle progression of ovarian cancer cells. Utilizing small interfering RNA (siRNA) to target MOB1A (siMOB1A) displays efficiency in blocking the cycle progression during the interphase of mitosis. The combined application of paclitaxel and siMOB1A holds promise in halting the cell cycle progression in ovarian cancer cells across different phases. Lipid nanoparticles delivering siMOB1A and paclitaxel (SPLNPs) were prepared by microfluidic technology. Then, the size distribution, zeta potential, morphology, and size stability of SPLNPs were characterized. Confocal laser scanning microscopy and flow cytometry were used to detect the cellular uptake ability of SPLNPs. RT-qPCR and Western blot were performed to evaluate the knockdown effect on MOB1A mRNA and protein levels. CCK-8 and colony formation assay were performed to evaluate the cytotoxicity of SPLNPs. A wound-healing assay was performed to detect the effect on cell migration. Flow cytometry was used to assess the effects on the cell cycle and apoptosis. Tumor-bearing mouse models were constructed to detect the distribution, anti-tumor effect, and biosafety in vivo. SPLNPs exhibited spherical morphology with an average diameter of approximately 113.5 nm and were efficiently internalized by ovarian cancer cells. The drug loading content was 7.50% for siMOB1A and 2.07% for paclitaxel. Through the RNA interference (RNAi) mechanisms facilitated by SPLNPs, effective suppression of MOB1A expression in ovarian cancer was achieved at both mRNA and protein levels. The knockdown efficiency reached 66.2% at the siMOB1A dose of 5 nM. Then, enhanced apoptosis of ovarian cancer cells was observed, accompanied by cell cycle modulation. Compared to siMOB1A and paclitaxel, SPLNPs showed superior cytotoxicity and effectively curbed the migration and proliferation ability of ovarian cancer cells. Additionally, in vivo experiments demonstrated that SPLNPs inhibit tumor growth, achieving an inhibition rate of approximately 65.23%. SPLNPs enabled the co-delivery of siMOB1A and PTX, resulting in enhanced antitumor activity and providing a promising co-delivery platform for ovarian cancer therapy.

title: TransGram for heterogeneity-aware transcriptome reconstruction from long read RNA-Seq data.
abstract: The advancement of long-read RNA sequencing technologies leads to a bright future for transcriptome analysis. Reconstructing alternative isoforms from long-read RNA data is crucial in transcriptomic studies and poses computational challenges. In this research, we study the heterogeneity of current long reads RNA-seq data, and categorize the sequencing data into two types according to the fraction of the alternative splicing events appeared in the extracted reliably supported sub-path of the splicing graph. Leveraging the heterogeneity, we develop TransGram, an algorithm to reconstruct transcriptome from long RNA-seq reads, which employs the traditional assemble strategy to reconstruct the transcript-representing paths within the splicing graph, and incorporates a machine-learning-based model trained on splice graph-derived features to eliminate false positive transcripts. TransGram supports both annotation-free and annotation-guided modes. Comprehensive evaluations across multiple datasets and conditions demonstrate that TransGram consistently outperforms widely used tools StringTie2, IsoQuant, Bambu, and ESPRESSO, in terms of precision and recall.

title: Col23a1 acts as an ECM-resident signal to drive DDR1-p38/ERK-dependent EMT in antimony-induced pulmonary fibrosis.
abstract: Antimony (Sb) exposure causes pulmonary fibrosis, but the molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Using a chronic Sb exposure mouse model combined with single-cell RNA sequencing, we identified Col23a1 as a highly and specifically expressed collagen in alveolar epithelial type II (AEC II) cells, with its expression correlating with epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Further analysis demonstrated that Col23a1 was enriched in the extracellular matrix (ECM), where it engaged discoidin domain receptor 1 (DDR1) to activate p38 and ERK1/2 phosphorylation, thereby driving EMT in AECs. Protein-protein interaction screening identified P4HA1 as a Col23a1-interacting candidate and that molecular docking supported a potential interaction. Functionally, P4HA1 stabilized Col23a1 and promoted its ECM deposition, while DDR1-p38/ERK signaling reciprocally sustained P4HA1 expression, forming a self-amplifying positive feedback loop. Pharmacological inhibition of DDR1 or p38/ERK and P4HA1 knockdown each attenuated Sb-induced EMT in AECs. Importantly, AEC-specific Col23a1 knockdown via AAV6-SPC-shCol23a1 in mice substantially reduced fibrotic remodeling and EMT in vivo, and ECM from Col23a1-knockdown lungs failed to induce EMT in naïve epithelial cells, confirming that ECM-resident Col23a1 is the functional component driving this fibrotic signal. Collectively, these findings establish a Col23a1-DDR1-p38/ERK self-amplifying axis as a driver of Sb-induced pulmonary fibrosis, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding the pulmonary toxicity of Sb and identifying this axis as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Coupling cellular trajectories and RNA kinetics on continuous expression manifolds with ManifoldVelo
abstract: Jointly recovering pseudotime and RNA velocity from static single-cell transcriptomes requires reconciling global trajectory structure with local expression changes, particularly in complex cycles and branching differentiation. Here we introduce ManifoldVelo, a topology-conditioned framework that jointly learns cellular coordinates, continuous RNA trajectories and regulatory kinetics. Derivatives of unspliced and spliced RNA trajectories are matched to transcription-splicing-degradation dynamics, including between observed cells, allowing expression reconstruction, cellular ordering and kinetic estimation to inform one another. ManifoldVelo recovers pseudotime across all evaluated single-cell trajectory types, including cyclic, multibranch and smooth non-branching trajectories. ManifoldVelo achieves the best pseudotime recovery among compared methods in multipeak cyclic simulations and the highest directional agreement for spliced RNA velocity in both multipeak cyclic and branching simulations. Real-data analyses support phase prediction across experimental plates and differentiation trajectories consistent with pancreatic developmental stages and marker expression. Its central advantage is the joint recovery of temporal position and local dynamics across distinct trajectory structures within a reusable dynamic reference. New cells are assigned pseudotime and velocity predictions from spliced RNA alone, without refitting the reference model. ManifoldVelo provides a foundation for dynamic cell atlases that transfer learned temporal and kinetic information to new samples.

title: Emerging roles of lncRNA-derived micropeptides in cancer: functional relationships with parental lncRNAs and clinical implications.
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have traditionally been regarded as non-protein-coding transcripts. However, accumulating evidence demonstrates that many lncRNAs contain small open reading frames (sORFs) that are actively translated into functional micropeptides. In cancer, these lncRNA-derived micropeptides regulate diverse hallmarks, including cell proliferation and apoptosis, metabolic reprogramming, metastasis, angiogenesis, and immune evasion. Mechanistically, they modulate enzymatic activity, protein complex assembly, RNA stability, splicing programs, and the subcellular localization of interacting partners. Notably, parental lncRNAs and their encoded micropeptides can exert concordant or divergent biological effects on tumor progression through distinct molecular pathways, highlighting the need to validate the functions of the RNA transcript and the translated peptide independently. Despite recent advances, distinguishing truly functional micropeptides from widespread but nonfunctional translation products and separating RNA-mediated from peptide-mediated effects remain major challenges. Emerging clinical evidence further suggests that lncRNA-derived micropeptides hold promise as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers. In this review, we systematically explore the functional roles and molecular mechanisms of lncRNA-derived micropeptides across major cancer hallmarks, compare the concordant and divergent biological outcomes of parental lncRNAs and their encoded micropeptides, and discuss their clinical potential as biomarkers and therapeutic targets alongside the current limitations that must be addressed for translational application.

title: Acute Pilon Fracture as a Clinical Model for Posttraumatic Osteoarthritis: A Feasibility Pilot Study of Synovial Fluid miR-146a Expression.
abstract: Posttraumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) is a frequent and debilitating sequela of intraarticular ankle fractures that progresses more rapidly than primary osteoarthritis. Pilon fractures demonstrate among the highest rates of PTOA and represent an attractive clinical model for studying early biological mechanisms of posttraumatic joint degeneration. Emerging evidence suggests dysregulated inflammation following intraarticular injury contributes to PTOA pathogenesis. miR-146a is a microRNA and a regulator of inflammatory signaling and cartilage homeostasis that has been implicated in osteoarthritis biology; however, its role in human PTOA following pilon fractures remains undefined. This prospective pilot study enrolled 5 adults (18-60 years) with acute closed unilateral pilon fractures. Bilateral ankle synovial fluid aspiration was performed at the time of definitive fixation. The contralateral uninjured ankle served as an internal control. Synovial fluid samples were obtained a mean of 14 days (range, 11-19) following injury. Four patients underwent staged temporary external fixation prior to definitive fixation, whereas 1 patient was managed with splint immobilization. Samples were processed for small RNA analysis and inflammatory protein quantification. miR-146a expression and concentrations of pro-inflammatory cytokines were compared between injured and uninjured ankles. Bilateral ankle synovial fluid aspiration was successful in all 5 patients. miR-146a was detectable in all injured and contralateral uninjured ankle samples. Mean miR-146a expression was lower in injured ankles compared with contralateral uninjured controls (0.43 ± 0.59 vs 1.00 ± 1.05; mean paired difference, -0.57 [95%CI, -1.21 to 0.08]; P = .07). Exploratory descriptive analyses demonstrated inverse correlations between miR-146a expression and concentrations of interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, IL-8, and tumor necrosis factor α. Synovial fluid aspiration and miR-146a quantification following acute pilon fracture were feasible in all participants. miR-146a was detectable in both injured and contralateral uninjured ankles in all samples. Further study is warranted to characterize synovial miRNA expression and inflammatory signaling following pilon fracture. Level IV, prognostic.

title: Uncovering cardiac molecular remodelling in racing Thoroughbreds with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common arrhythmia in both humans and horses, with a comparable prevalence of ~2%. In horses, AF is a major cause of poor athletic performance and linked to sudden cardiac death, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. To investigate transcriptomic remodelling associated with spontaneous paroxysmal AF (PAF). Case-control study. We performed RNA sequencing on left atrial (LA) tissue from three Thoroughbred racehorses with PAF and four matched controls. All horses were euthanised due to musculoskeletal reasons. Cell type deconvolution was performed with BayesPrism. The differential expression analysis was performed with EdgeR. Alternative splicing analysis was performed with SUPPA2.
