Cell-type deconvolution revealed a modest, non-significant shift towards increased fibroblast and immune cell proportions in PAF, but not enough to account for widespread transcriptional changes. 1400 of the 12,012 included genes were considered significantly differentially expressed (Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value <0.05). These genes included ion channels, calcium-handling proteins, and conduction-related genes. In addition, several genes directly involved in cardiac muscle contraction and mitochondrial energy metabolism were differentially expressed. Alternative splicing analysis revealed over 20 significantly altered events, including skipped exons in genes with potential relevance to cardiac function and remodelling. The number of biological replicates was modest. Overall, despite no major changes in cell composition, the findings highlight intrinsic structural and molecular changes in the LA of PAF-affected horses. This study provides the first transcriptomic and splicing analysis of atrial tissue in racehorses with PAF, revealing molecular remodelling consistent with mechanisms of arrhythmia maintenance and suggesting potential targets for further functional investigation.

title: A Retinal Matrix Stiffening Model Reveals FAK-Dependent Mechanotransduction in Pericytes Underlies Vascular Destabilization.
abstract: Pericyte loss, an early hallmark of diabetic retinopathy (DR), is linked to hyperglycemia and inflammation, whereas the contribution of mechanical changes in the retina remains unclear. We define design parameters for an iPSC-derived microphysiological system (MPS) comprising pericyte-endothelial capillary networks embedded in a dynamically stiffening hydrogel engineered to reproduce matrix stiffening in a controlled, human-relevant context. Microrheology of Ins2Akita mouse retinas revealed increased storage modulus in perivascular regions at a diabetic timepoint coincident with reduced pericyte coverage and vascular remodeling, establishing a stiffness magnitude used to inform the design of the MPS. In the MPS, progressive matrix stiffening alone, in the absence of hyperglycemic exposure, was sufficient to induce analogous vascular defects and to suppress pericyte expression of NOTCH3, HEY1, JAG1, and N-cadherin in a focal adhesion kinase (FAK)-dependent manner. Inhibition of FAK restored pericyte signaling and vascular integrity in stiffened conditions without altering soft controls, identifying a FAK-dependent mechanotransduction as a druggable target. Single-cell RNA-sequencing of human diabetic retinas validated enrichment of focal-adhesion components and alterations in Notch-pathway transcripts in pericytes. These findings establish a human MPS showing matrix stiffening as a key regulator of pericyte-mediated vascular stabilization and nominate it and FAK-dependent mechanotransduction as targets to prevent DR pathogenesis.

title: The Role of Akt Signaling in Regulating Developmental Plasticity in Horned Beetles.
abstract: Developmental plasticity in response to nutrition is widespread across taxa and has been the subject of numerous studies, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying tissue-specific plasticity remain poorly understood. The insulin/insulin-like signaling (IIS) pathway regulates growth in many insects, including the horned beetle Digitonthophagus gazella, a species characterized by male head horn polyphenism. Here, we investigate the role of Akt, a central protein that acts directly upstream of the IIS transcription factor FOXO, a known regulator of horn development. We hypothesized that Akt contributes to nutrition-responsive trait development, acting in concert with FOXO and other members of the IIS. Using RNA interference (RNAi), we knocked down Akt and assessed its effects on traits that differ in a sex- and nutrition-specific manner. AktRNAi resulted in a reduction in growth across multiple traits, including overall body size, foretibia, female prothoracic protrusions and male head horns. Transcriptomic analyses of horn tissue across nutrition conditions further showed differential expression of Akt-interacting genes, suggesting that complex interactions across IIS pathway components and additional regulatory networks coordinate nutrition-responsive growth. Together, these results identify Akt as a key regulator of context‑dependent, trait‑ and sex‑specific plasticity in D. gazella, and highlight the complexity of plastic responses and the need for further investigation.

title: An integrative multi-omic analysis of skeletal muscle in response to disuse and recovery resistance training in resistance trained and untrained young adults.
abstract: We previously reported that resistance trained (T) and untrained (UT) individuals exhibit similar targeted molecular responses in skeletal muscle following two weeks of leg immobilization and eight weeks of subsequent recovery resistance training (RT). The present analysis examined the skeletal muscle transcriptome, microRNA (miR)-ome, and proteome responses in a subset of these participants (N = 8 T and N = 8 UT). Vastus lateralis biopsies were obtained at baseline (PRE), after the 2-wk immobilization protocol (DIS), and after 8-wk of recovery RT (REC-RT). Tissue RNA and protein were subjected to RNA- and miR-sequencing and proteomics, respectively. Analyses included: (i) group and time differential expression (DE) and pathway enrichment for each independent -ome; (ii) multi-omics integration to reveal modules across the -omes; and (iii) leave one out cross-validated linear regression modeling (LOOCV) to reveal key features predictive of atrophy and hypertrophy. Most differentially expressed (DE) RNAs or differentially abundant (DA) proteins were time-driven rather than training status-driven. In all participants, the transcriptome was most responsive to disuse (PRE-to-DIS: 2047 DE mRNAs; 3 DE miRs; 10 DA proteins) while the transcriptome and proteome were both responsive to recovery RT (DIS-to-REC-RT: 446 DE mRNAs; 0 DE miR; 415 DA proteins). Pathways analyses revealed proteostasis and DNA repair with disuse atrophy, whereas striated muscle contraction, transcriptional regulation, and rRNA expression were enriched with recovery RT. Integrative analyses identified SLIT-ROBO signaling as a potentially novel axis in disuse atrophy, driven predominantly by transcriptomic changes, whereas enrichment of striated muscle contraction pathways in recovery RT was supported by coordinated mRNA and protein regulation. Via LOOCV, the 10 top predictors of disuse atrophy were RNAs (8 protein coding) primarily related to mitochondrial function and protein trafficking, while 9 of the top 10 predictors of recovery RT hypertrophy were RNAs (8 protein coding) related to membrane dynamics, ECM/cytoskeletal organization, and translation initiation. This integrative multi-omic approach reiterates that disuse atrophy and recovery RT-induced hypertrophy elicit similar molecular responses in T and UT individuals, highlighting distinct molecular signatures governing skeletal muscle atrophy and recovery hypertrophy independent of training status.

title: GTSE1 promotes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma stemness via the Hippo signaling pathway.
abstract: Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are pivotal in driving tumorigenesis, metastasis, and resistance to multiple drugs. In this study, genes associated with stemness were identified, and the effects of GTSE1 on esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) stemness and its underlying mechanism were elucidated. We utilized a trained stemness index model, adapted from a one-class logistic regression (OCLR) machine-learning approach, to evaluate the stemness indices of ESCC samples based on gene expression-based stemness index (mRNAsi). Subsequent algorithmic and single-cell subtype analyses confirmed the predictive capability of the mRNAsi and pinpointed GTSE1 as a potential target. Loss-of-function and gain-of-function genetic experiments were conducted to evaluate the influence of GTSE1 on ESCC self-renewal and tumor progression. Mechanistic investigations involved RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), immunofluorescence, coimmunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and so on. Additionally, the efficacy of verteporfin (a Hippo pathway inhibitor) was evaluated in vitro and vivo. The analysis of the mRNAsi in bulk RNA-seq and single RNA-seq data reveals elevated expression of GTSE1 in the high mRNAsi subgroup and clusters of highly malignant single cells. Functional studies demonstrate that the depletion of GTSE1 hinders self-renewal and progression of ESCC. Mechanistically, GTSE1 modulates the Hippo signaling pathway. GTSE1 regulates cytoskeletal tension and interacts with LATS1 to facilitate its ubiquitination and degradation, thereby reducing YAP phosphorylation and promoting its nuclear translocation. Treatment with verteporfin, significantly impairs self-renewal and progression, particularly in cells with high GTSE1 expression. This study underscores the association of GTSE1 with the stemness of ESCC, highlighting its interaction with LATS1 to regulate nuclear localization of YAP and modulate the Hippo signaling pathway. Consequently, GTSE1 emerges as a promising therapeutic target for ESCC.

title: Clinical utility of Circulating Long Non-Coding RNAs in indeterminate thyroid nodules.
abstract: Indeterminate cytology results (Bethesda categories III and IV) from fine-needle aspiration (FNA) create challenges in clinical decision-making. This study evaluated the expression and diagnostic utility of selected long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in cell-free plasma from patients with indeterminate thyroid nodules. Prospective, single-center study. Nine candidate long non-coding RNA were selected from a curated disease database. A total of 126 individuals with solitary thyroid nodules were enrolled. RNA was extracted from plasma, FNA, and tissue samples and expression levels were measured using quantitative real-time PCR. In the discovery cohort, patients with benign and malignant nodules confirmed by histopathology, were used to determine optimal cut-off values through receiver operating characteristic analysis. Spearman correlation analyses were performed to assess concordance between plasma and FNA/tissue expression. In the validation phase, significantly altered markers were applied to indeterminate nodules to assess diagnostic performance. In the discovery cohort, PVT1, MALAT1, and BANCR were significantly upregulated in malignant compared with benign nodules (P < 0.0001). Significant positive correlations were observed between plasma and FNA expression for PVT1 (r = 0.7095), MALAT1 (r = 0.5487), and BANCR (r = 0.6792), and between plasma and tissue expression for PVT1 (r = 0.7673), MALAT1 (r = 0.5284), and BANCR (r = 0.6864) (P < 0.0001). In the Bethesda III/IV validation cohort, only PVT1 retained diagnostic utility, with 76% sensitivity, 87.5% specificity, 85% positive predictive value, and 80% negative predictive value, whereas MALAT1 and BANCR did not demonstrate significant diagnostic performance. Circulating PVT1 expression in plasma may serve as a useful non-invasive biomarker for distinguishing benign from malignant indeterminate thyroid nodules.

title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses identify key metabolites and genes in sepsis-associated acute lung injury.
abstract: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury (SALI) is a life-threatening pulmonary complication of sepsis with high mortality. This study aimed to prioritize serum metabolites and genes potentially involved in SALI by integrating multi-omics datasets. A rat SALI model treated with Xuanbai Chengqi Decoction (XCD) was subjected to untargeted serum metabolomics. Bulk and single-cell RNA-seq datasets were retrieved from GEO, and metabolite-related GWAS statistics were obtained from IEU OpenGWAS. scPagwas mapped metabolite genetic signals to cell populations; hdWGCNA identified cell signature genes. Candidate genes were filtered by overlapping bulk DEGs, ten machine-learning models and expression validation. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, cell -cell communication, pseudotime and scTenifoldKnk virtual knockdown analyses were performed. Oleoylcarnitine showed the strongest genetic association with T cells. Cross-platform integration prioritized GIMAP4 and RCBTB2 as hub genes, with WBP2 retained for further validation. Their expression correlated with altered immune infiltration, especially eosinophils, and the three-gene profiles shared 62 biological processes. SALI exhibited increased number and strength of cell interactions compared with isolated sepsis. Five T-cell subsets were identified, and virtual knockdown of hub genes modified regulation of eight DEGs. Oleoylcarnitine-associated metabolic changes are correlated with T-cell dysregulation mediated by GIMAP4, RCBTB2, and WBP2 in SALI. These findings are descriptive, and further experiments are required to establish causal relationships.

title: Long COVID shows IL-1 pathway dysregulation without a discrete circulating biomarker signature.
abstract: Long COVID (LC) is characterized by persistent and, often, disabling symptoms, yet its biological basis remains unclear. Multiple mechanisms, including immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, and persistence of SARS-CoV-2 components, have been proposed, although it is unknown whether these define distinct biological subtypes or overlapping processes. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 312 individuals, including 139 people with LC (PWLC), 99 COVID-19-recovered controls (both groups sampled a median of 8 months after primary SARS-CoV-2 infection), and 74 uninfected controls, from an unvaccinated population, thereby minimizing major sources of biological and epidemiological variability. Circulating immune and endothelial biomarkers and plasma SARS-CoV-2 RNA were assessed, together with serological signatures associated with herpesvirus reactivation and SARS-CoV-2-specific humoral responses. Associations with symptom persistence were analyzed using multivariable models and machine learning approaches. Most soluble biomarker differences primarily distinguished previously infected individuals from uninfected controls rather than PWLC from recovered participants. Increased IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1RA) levels, together with reduced IL-1β/IL-1RA ratios, were the immune alterations most strongly associated with LC, while P-selectin was the endothelial marker showing a suggestive association with symptom persistence. Plasma SARS-CoV-2 RNA was detected at low and comparable frequencies in PWLC and recovered individuals, while Ct values tended to be lower among RNA-positive PWLC not reaching statistical difference. Epstein-Barr virus serological profiles were characterized by lower latency- and higher reactivation-associated responses in PWLC, whereas SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody levels were comparable between groups. Integrated biomarker profiles discriminated prior infection more effectively than LC status, and expansion to multimodal predictors did not clearly improve discrimination between PWLC and recovered participants. Overall, LC was associated with overlapping immune, endothelial, and virological alterations rather than discrete biomarker-defined subtypes.

title: Inflammatory signature of subcutaneous fat after weight loss and regain in women undergoing repeated bariatric surgery.
abstract: Repeated metabolic-bariatric surgery (MBS, r-BS) represents 10-25% of all MBS and is commonly-performed for weight regain after prior significant weight-loss. It remains unclear how adipose tissue adapts to surgically-induced weight-loss-regain in obesity. We hypothesized that compared to primary bariatric surgery (p-BS), women undergoing r-BS exhibit a distinct adipose tissue signature. Subcutaneous/visceral adipose tissues (SAT/VAT, respectively) from female MBS patients were assessed histologically/molecularly/functionally (activation of human microglia cells by SAT-secretome). Elective MBS in a public university hospital. Women undergoing either p-BS, or r-BS with documented >15% weight-loss after prior MBS. MBS. Inflammation in SAT. Women undergoing r-BS (n=21) trended to be older than those undergoing p-BS (n=35)(47.2 vs. 40.5y, p=0.06), with a lower BMI (42.3 vs. 45.6 kg/m2, respectively, p=0.103), and a trend for improved cardiometabolic risk parameters (fasting insulin, CRP and HDL-c). Adipocyte size, adipose tissue fibrosis, macrophage and crown-like structures abundance were similar, while mast-cells were slightly more prevalent in r-BS. Single-nucleus RNA-seq-based deconvolution algorithm applied unto bulk RNA-seq confirmed the absence of a major shift in adipose tissue cell-type composition. Yet, RNA-seq revealed unique transcriptome of r-BS SAT, with activation of inflammatory pathways. Consistently, SAT explants from r-BS secreted higher protein concentrations of NFκB-regulated cytokines IL6/IL8. Functional impact of the more inflammatory-secretome was suggested by its increased ability to inflammatory-activate human microglia cells. Prior BS-induced weight-loss and subsequent regain in women is associated with inflammatory transcriptome and secretome of SAT that can activate cultured human microglia cells.

title: Compensatory activation of PI3K/AKT signaling and apoptosis-associated protein expression in pulmonary hypertension-induced right ventricular dysfunction.
abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive cardiopulmonary disorder marked by increased pulmonary vascular resistance and poor prognosis. Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is the principal determinant of mortality in patients with PH; however, the role of the PI3K/AKT pathway in PH-induced RV remodeling remains poorly defined. The present study generated a hypobaric hypoxia-induced PH model in C57BL/6J mice. Echocardiography, histology, reverse transcription-quantitative PCR, western blotting and immunofluorescence staining were employed to assess RV structure, apoptosis-associated protein expression and fibrosis, while RNA sequencing was used to identify enriched signaling pathways. In parallel, H9C2 cardiomyocytes were treated with angiotensin II (Ang II) with or without the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 to evaluate apoptosis-associated protein expression changes. PH model mice developed RV dysfunction characterized by increased Bax and decreased Bcl-2 expression, accompanied by fibrosis. Transcriptomic analysis revealed significant enrichment of the PI3K/AKT pathway in RV tissues from PH model mice compared with control mice. Pharmacological inhibition of PI3K/AKT signaling with LY294002 further upregulated Bax and downregulated Bcl-2 in Ang II-treated H9C2 cells. In conclusion, PI3K/AKT pathway enrichment may represent a compensatory but insufficient response during PH-induced RV remodeling, and its precise modulation may offer a potential therapeutic strategy for PH-associated RV failure.

title: Single-cell transcriptome analysis of muscle and blood tissues from a patient with a rare homozygous ANO5 variant causing limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type R12.
abstract: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type R12 (LGMD R12) is a recessive genetic myopathy, typically caused by pathogenic variants in anoctamin-5 (ANO5), which encodes a multipass membrane protein localized to the sarcolemma and sarcoplasmic reticulum of muscle fibers. Effective therapeutic strategies for LGMD R12 remain elusive. A comprehensive analytical framework is required to dissect the cellular and molecular changes underlying this disease. The ANO5 variant in the patient and his family members was validated by Sanger sequencing. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing analysis on biceps brachii muscle tissue (MUS) and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy controls (HCs) and a patient who was homozygous for the pathogenic variant in exon 10 of ANO5 (c.898dupA, p.Ile300fs). Immunofluorescence staining was conducted to validate key findings from the single-cell transcriptome analysis. In the MUS cell atlas , we observed a significant loss of type I muscle fibers in the patient with LGMD R12. Accordingly, immunofluorescence staining revealed a dramatic loss of MYH7+ cells (MYH7+, a marker of type I muscle fibers) compared with those in controls. Glycolytic pathway activity and cellular metabolic activity were significantly downregulated, suggesting that they are two transcriptomic signatures in the muscle tissue of this patient. In addition, muscle progenitor cells from the patient exhibited impaired differentiation capacity, failing to generate mature myocytes. In both MUS and PBMCs, we also observed heightened immune crosstalk accompanied by significant activation of pathways such as LGALS9-CD45/CD44 and ANXA1-FPR1, suggesting immunological activation in this patient. LGMD R12 with pathogenic ANO5 variants is a rare genetic disease. Our transcriptome and experimental analyses revealed dramatic cellular and molecular changes in affected tissue at the single-cell resolution in a patient with LGMD R12. This study provides valuable insights into the underlying mechanisms and potential development of interventions for this recessive genetic myopathy.

title: Identification of an S-nitrosylation-Related Gene Signature for Alzheimer's Disease via Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Profiling.
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with limited early-stage diagnostic tools and disease-modifying therapies. While Post-Translational Modifications (PTMs) are known to regulate AD pathogenesis, the comprehensive landscape of Snitrosylation and its role in driving cerebrovascular and metabolic dysfunction remains poorly understood. Three independent bulk transcriptomic datasets (GSE138260, GSE29378, GSE5281) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) profiles (GSE157827) were integrated to systematically evaluate PTM enrichment patterns using single-sample Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (ssGSEA). A Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) network was constructed to identify hub genes, which were further validated for cell-type specificity and functional pathways. Among the evaluated PTM-related gene sets, the S-nitrosylation-related signature showed significant enrichment in AD tissues. A five-gene hub signature-HSP90AB1, ITGA6, KLF4, SOX2, and VIM-that significantly correlates with S-nitrosylation activity was identified. Specifically, SOX2, VIM, KLF4, and ITGA6 were significantly upregulated in AD, while HSP90AB1 was downregulated. Notably, scRNA-seq analysis revealed that VIM and ITGA6 are specifically upregulated in brain endothelial cells, aligning with the enrichment of focal adhesion and cell adhesion pathways. Conversely, downregulation of HSP90AB1 was associated with impaired oxidative phosphorylation and proteostasis. This study identifies S-nitrosylation-related transcriptional signatures associated with AD and highlights potential roles of VIM, ITGA6, and HSP90AB1 in endothelial dysfunction and metabolic regulation, providing new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying AD pathogenesis. A five-gene S-nitrosylation signature (HSP90AB1, ITGA6, KLF4, SOX2, VIM) associated with AD was identified; the endothelial enrichment of VIM and ITGA6 and the loss of HSP90AB1 nominate these three genes as priority candidates for experimental validation and, potentially, therapeutic targeting.

title: Spatially resolved GR-TGFβ co-activation underlies cell-type-specific signalling in triple-negative breast cancer.
abstract: The clinical relevance of glucocorticoid receptor (GR) activation in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains controversial. While preclinical studies link GR activity to tumour progression, clinical data are inconsistent, despite the routine use of synthetic glucocorticoids as supportive therapy during chemotherapy. This paradox suggests that GR signalling may be highly context- and cell-type-specific within the tumour microenvironment. Understanding the spatial organisation and molecular partners of glucocorticoid receptor signalling is therefore essential to clarify its functional and clinical impact. We comprehensively characterised spatially resolved GR expression and signalling across malignant, stromal, and immune compartments in human triple-negative breast cancer specimens. GR protein expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry, while spatial transcriptomics was used to resolve compartment-specific transcriptional programs. Stereological confocal microscopy enabled quantitative analysis of GR and transforming growth factor beta receptor 2 (TGFBR2) co-expression at single-cell resolution in a spatial distribution. These spatial data were integrated with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing datasets to define signalling states, ligand dependence, and pathway interactions. Intercellular communication analyses were applied to identify signalling at tumour-immune interfaces. Functional relevance was assessed using in vitro migration assays and transcriptome sequencing following glucocorticoid stimulation with or without TGFBR2 inhibition. Associations with clinical outcome were evaluated using survival analyses of pathway-correlated gene signatures. GR expression was enriched within the tumour microenvironment and associated with shared gene programs across tumour and stromal populations, prominently involving TGFβ pathway components. Stereological protein analyses revealed increased GR activation at invasive tumour edges and adjacent normal epithelium, accompanied by marked co-localisation with TGFBR2. Spatial transcriptomics demonstrated predominantly ligand-independent GR activation in tumour cells, whereas tumour-infiltrating immune cells displayed ligand-dependent signalling linked to local corticosteroid metabolism. Intercellular communication analyses identified enhanced GR-TGFβ signalling at the tumour-immune interface. Functionally, glucocorticoid-induced tumour cell migration was abolished by TGFBR2 inhibition. Clinically, GR-correlated and glucocorticoid-induced TGFβ gene signatures were associated with reduced overall survival. These findings reveal spatially regulated, cell-type-specific GR-TGFβ co-activation in TNBC. This signalling axis underlies pro-migratory tumour behaviour and adverse clinical outcome, identifying a potential prognostic marker and therapeutic vulnerability with important implications for glucocorticoid use in cancer treatment.

title: Targeting the circ_0042819-PLA2G6 axis sensitizes multiple myeloma to proteasome inhibitors through ferroptosis induction.
abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a refractory plasma cell neoplasm characterized by frequent development of drug resistance, leading to poor clinical outcomes. Activation of ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has emerged as a promising cancer therapeutic strategy. In this study, we show that the circular RNA circ_0042819 exhibits high expression in both bone marrow and plasma samples from MM patients, with its overexpression strongly associated with disease progression and unfavorable prognosis. Mechanistically, circ_0042819 directly interacts with Up-frameshift protein 1 (UPF1) in MM cells, and the circ_0042819-UPF1 complex upregulates the expression of phospholipase A2 group VI (PLA2G6) via interacting with, and thus stabilizing, its mRNA. Furthermore, the circ_0042819-PLA2G6 axis suppresses ferroptosis through phospholipid remodeling in MM cells. Importantly, depletion of circ_0042819 or PLA2G6 enhances MM sensitivity to proteasome inhibitors (bortezomib and carfilzomib) by promoting ferroptosis both in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that circ_0042819 is a potential non-invasive biomarker for the diagnosis and prognosis of MM, and that inhibition of the circ_0042819-PLA2G6 axis can mitigate the resistance of MM to proteasome inhibitors through ferroptosis sensitization, thus suggesting a novel therapeutic approach.

title: An integrated MRI-pathology model for predicting response to TACE combined with targeted therapy and immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: The efficacy of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by variable responses. We aimed to develop and validate an integrated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-pathology model for response prediction and survival stratification (IMPRESS), which combines pretreatment MRI habitat radiomics and paired biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs) pathomics. This multicenter, retrospective study enrolled patients with unresectable HCC receiving TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy from January 2019 to December 2024. Eligibility required pretreatment MRI and paired biopsy WSIs within 1 month before therapy, Child-Pugh class A/B, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status ≤ 1, and at least one measurable intrahepatic lesion ≥ 1 cm. Patients with missing or poor-quality MRI or WSIs, prior locoregional or systemic HCC therapy, second malignancy, ECOG ≥ 2, or incomplete data were excluded. Habitat MRI radiomics, WSI pathomics, and clinical features were integrated into IMPRESS. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Single-cell analysis was performed to explore the biological basis of the IMPRESS predictions. Among 231 patients, 94 (40.7%) achieved a treatment response. IMPRESS achieved AUCs of 0.957 (95% CI: 0.931-1.0), 0.878 (95% CI: 0.789-0.966), and 0.875 (95% CI: 0.782-0.966) in the training, validation, and test cohorts, respectively. Predicted responders and non-responders showed significantly different overall survival in all cohorts (all p < 0.001). Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed distinct immune and proliferative patterns consistent with model predictions. IMPRESS model may provide a promising tool for pretreatment response prediction and survival risk stratification in unresectable HCC undergoing TACE-based combination therapy. Question Reliable pretreatment tools are needed to identify unresectable HCC patients likely to benefit from TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy. Findings An integrated MRI-pathology model combining habitat radiomics and deep-learning pathomics predicted treatment response, with validation and testing areas under the curve of 0.878 and 0.875. Clinical relevance The integrated model may support pretreatment response stratification for TACE-based triple therapy and help inform surveillance intensity or alternative treatment considerations, pending prospective validation.

title: Identification of potential pathogenic genes for lung adenocarcinoma induced by 6PPD-quinone through network toxicology and SHAP analysis.
abstract: Lung cancer continues to maintain a high mortality rate, with lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) being its most common type. As an emerging environmental pollutant, 6PPD-quinone is attracting increasing attention. Through network toxicology, we constructed a prognostic model and validated it with molecular docking and dynamics simulations, revealing its underlying molecular mechanisms. RNA-seq and clinical data of LUAD were obtained from the TCGA database, and differential expression analysis was performed using DESeq2. Putative targets of 6PPD-quinone were retrieved from DIGEP-Pred 2.0 and SEA databases, while LUAD-associated genes were collected from GeneCards, CTD, and OMIM. Overlapping genes with DEGs were identified as potential targets. Protein-protein interaction networks were constructed via STRING and visualized with Cytoscape. The hub genes were screened using four algorithms (Degree, EPC, MCC, MNC). GO and KEGG enrichment analyses were conducted on both potential and hub genes. A prognostic model was built based on Cox regression, with risk scores calculated for survival and independent prognostic analyses. SHAP analysis was applied to interpret feature contributions. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations assessed binding stability between 6PPD-quinone and key genes, and qPCR validated expression changes in BEAS-2B and A549 cells with or without 6PPD-quinone exposure. 6PPD-quinone-linked LUAD were used to identify 31 potential targets and screen 18 network hub genes. Through a seven-gene prognostic signature (GPI, FAM83D, KRT17, CTLA4, MAP3K8, SIX1, ABCC2) construction, clear stratification into high- and low-risk groups was achieved with significantly different survival rates (1-year AUC = 0.711). SHAP analysis highlighted GPI, FAM83D, KRT17, and ABCC2 as major pathogenic contributors. Molecular docking demonstrated stable binding between 6PPD-quinone and GPI, FAM83D, and ABCC2 (binding energies < -5 kcal/mol). Furthermore, MD simulations confirmed the stability of the ABCC2-ligand complex. qPCR validation confirmed that exposure to 6PPD-quinone markedly enhanced the expression of these genes in A549 cells. This study identifies GPI, FAM83D, and ABCC2 as potential pathogenic genes linking 6PPD-quinone exposure to LUAD, possibly through genetic dysregulation. The integrative network toxicology and SHAP-based approach provide a robust framework for uncovering environmental carcinogenesis mechanisms, offering new insights into the health risks of tire-derived pollutants.

title: Upregulation of NKAIN1 Predicts Poor Prognosis and Shapes Immune Infiltration in Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma: An Integrated Bioinformatic and Experimental Study.
abstract: This research sought to explore the expression profile, prognostic relevance, and immune- related functions of Sodium/Potassium Transporting ATPase Interacting 1 (NKAIN1) in Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma (UCEC) through integrated bioinformatic approaches followed by experimental validation. RNA-seq data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were analyzed to assess NKAIN1 expression across cancer types, with a specific comparison between UCEC and healthy tissues. Differential expression, survival outcomes, Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), immune infiltration patterns, Tumor Mutation Burden (TMB), mRNA stemness index (mRNAsi), and drug sensitivity correlations were evaluated using R packages. Samples with missing clinical data were excluded from the respective clinical correlation analyses. Protein- level expression was confirmed via the Human Protein Atlas (HPA) database, while mRNA levels were measured in UCEC cell lines (Ishikawa, KLE) and Endometrial Stromal Cells (ESC) by qRT-PCR. NKAIN1 was markedly elevated in UCEC tissues and cell lines compared to normal controls (p < 0.01). Higher NKAIN1 levels were associated with more advanced clinical stage, increased histological grade, and worse Overall Survival (OS), Progression-Free Survival (PFS), and Disease-Specific Survival (DSS) (p < 0.01). Multivariate Cox analysis identified NKAIN1 as an independent prognostic factor. GSEA revealed enrichment in immune-related pathways, cytokine interactions, and cell cycle regulation. NKAIN1 expression negatively correlated with immune score, Th17 cell infiltration, and TMB, but positively correlated with mRNAsi and certain immune checkpoint genes (e.g., LAG3). Drug sensitivity analysis associated NKAIN1 with response to Tamoxifen, 5-Fluorouracil, and other agents. Somatic mutations in NKAIN1 were rare (0.95%) in UCEC. The correlative findings suggest that NKAIN1 may serve as a novel prognostic biomarker in UCEC, with potential roles in tumor progression, immune evasion, and stemness maintenance. The correlations with immune infiltration and checkpoint genes highlight its relevance in tumor immunology. It is important to note that these are hypotheses generated from the correlative data, which require rigorous testing in future functional experiments. However, limitations include reliance on public databases, small experimental sample size, the retrospective nature of TCGA analyses, and lack of mechanistic validation. Additional studies are needed to clarify the functional routes and therapeutic relevance of NKAIN1 in UCEC. NKAIN1 is overexpressed in UCEC and correlates with unfavorable prognosis, an altered immune microenvironment, and treatment sensitivity. It stands as a promising biomarker for risk stratification and a possible candidate for further investigation in the context of personalized immunotherapy. Future research should focus on mechanistic insights and clinical validation of NKAIN1 in UCEC management.

title: Macrophage Contribution to Tumour Matrisome in Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: To investigate the direct contribution of macrophages to the tumour matrisome in human cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC), we established a three-dimensional spheroid-based coculture model incorporating CSCC cells, fibroblasts, and macrophages derived from the THP-1 cell line. This model also enabled comparison between interleukin-4-induced (M2-like) and interferon-γ-induced (M1-like) macrophages. RNA sequencing revealed differential expression of matrisome-associated genes, including the pro-tumorigenic chemokines CXCL6, CCL18, and CCL13, which were associated with M2-like macrophages, whereas CXCL9 was associated with the M1-like phenotype. NanoString analysis of CSCC tumours and normal skin confirmed increased expression of these chemokines in CSCC. The spheroid model also demonstrated substantial macrophage plasticity, particularly among initially M1-like macrophages. Mass-spectrometry-based proteomics identified galectin-9 (LGALS9) as the most prominently increased core-matrisome protein in spheroids. Immunohistochemical analysis of clinical samples confirmed significantly greater galectin-9 accumulation in CSCC metastases than in non-metastatic primary tumours. Analysis of publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing data showed that LGALS9 expression was associated with CD86high macrophages and further supported the macrophage origin of the identified chemokines. High LGALS9 expression correlated with reduced numbers of CD8+ T lymphocytes and increased expression of the galectin-9 receptor HAVCR2 (TIM-3) and T-cell exhaustion markers in CD8+ cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that galectin-9 may suppress CD8+ T-cell responses and contribute to an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. High galectin-9 expression may therefore serve as a marker of altered immune regulation in CSCC, particularly in metastatic disease.

title: Senescence-related immunosuppressive gene MFAP2 orchestrates stromal-immune crosstalk and immunotherapy resistance in gastric cancer.
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with poor prognosis and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) resistance mediated by immune escape. Senescence-related immunosuppressive genes (SRIGs) regulate the tumor microenvironment (TME); however, their hub genes and prognostic value in GC remain unclear. This study aimed to identify hub SRIGs and explore their significance. Transcriptomic, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic data of GC were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus databases. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and Pearson correlation analysis were used to screen for SRIGs. Eight machine learning algorithms identified the hub SRIG, which was validated by RT-qPCR, immunohistochemistry, and clinical samples. Pseudotime trajectory, CellChat, and molecular docking analyses were used to explore the underlying mechanisms and potential drugs. A pan-cancer analysis was used to verify its generalizability. A senescence-related immunosuppressive signature was constructed, stratifying GC into two subtypes with distinct TME and prognosis. Microfibril-associated protein 2 (MFAP2) was identified as the hub SRIG, significantly upregulated in GC, and an independent prognostic risk factor. It was specifically expressed in extracellular matrix cancer-associated fibroblasts (eCAFs), driving their differentiation and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. MFAP2⁺ eCAFs promoted M2 macrophage polarization via CSF1-CSF1R and C3-C3AR1 axes, mediating immune escape and ICI resistance. AZD4547 and MK-2461 were potential targeted drugs. Pan-cancer analysis confirmed the ubiquitous oncogenic role of MFAP2. MFAP2 is a hub SRIG linking eCAFs, ECM remodeling, and immune escape in GC. It serves as a reliable prognostic and ICI resistance predictor and potential therapeutic target, providing a basis for precision therapy in GC.

title: Aberrant expression of HERV-K envelope in lymphoma represents an opportunity for novel treatments.
abstract: Human endogenous retrovirus K (HERV-K/HML-2) is a human-specific endogenous retrovirus family that maintains intact open reading frames and is aberrantly expressed in multiple cancers. We tested whether HERV-K, specifically its envelope (Env) protein, marks clinically relevant diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) states and serves as a tractable immunotherapeutic target. Locus-level transposable element (TE) and HERV expression was quantified in two independent DLBCL RNA-seq cohorts using curated TE annotation and a uniform alignment/counting workflow. Env transcript and protein expression (including cell-surface localization) was validated in lymphoma cell lines using RT-qPCR, immunoblotting, and flow cytometry. Functional relevance was assessed by siRNA-mediated Env knockdown. Candidate extracellular linear epitopes were predicted in silico and synthesized for serological and phage display assays. Anti-Env camelid VHHs were isolated, humanized, and tested for binding, antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), and antigen-dependent internalization. TE transcripts stratified DLBCL into clinically distinct subgroups, and high HERV-K expression associated with an interferon/viral-mimicry program. Env RNA was detected in patient tumors and cell lines, and the protein was detected on the surface of a subset of lymphoma cell lines, in which Env knockdown reduced proliferation. A humanized heavy-chain antibody (FF-01) bound surface Env, induced selective ADCC in Env-positive models (reporter and primary NK-cell assays), and underwent rapid antigen-dependent internalization. HERV-K activity identifies biologically meaningful DLBCL states and exposes a targetable surface antigen. FF-01 provides proof of principle for antibody-based strategies against HERV-K Env, including ADCC- and ADC-oriented approaches.

title: Integrative bioinformatics and experimental validation of the prognostic and functional relevance of XDH and ITPA in non-small cell lung cancer.
abstract: Purine metabolism has been implicated in tumor biology and immune regulation, but the clinical and biological relevance of purine metabolism-related genes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains incompletely defined. Transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and the Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) project, together with TCGA clinical data, were analyzed to identify differentially expressed purine metabolism-related genes and assess their prognostic associations. Immune infiltration was evaluated using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA), and single-cell transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to characterize the cellular context of candidate genes. Stemness features and drug sensitivity were assessed using transcriptome-based computational models. XDH and ITPA protein expression was examined by Western blotting and immunohistochemistry (IHC) in an independent NSCLC cohort and in cell models. Stable knockdown of XDH or ITPA was performed in H1299 cells, with key functional findings further evaluated in A549 cells. Cisplatin sensitivity was assessed using cell-viability dose-response assays in H1299 and A549 cells. Several purine metabolism-related genes were upregulated in NSCLC and associated with overall survival (OS). XDH and ITPA showed higher protein expression in tumor tissues and were associated with adverse clinicopathological features and poorer survival. Higher expression of these genes was also associated with altered immune infiltration patterns. The messenger RNA-based stemness index (mRNAsi) was associated with ITPA and XDH expression in different directions, whereas higher XDH expression was associated with higher predicted half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values for cisplatin. Knockdown of XDH or ITPA attenuated proliferative, clonogenic, migratory, and invasive phenotypes in H1299 cells, with key findings reproduced in A549 cells. XDH knockdown also reduced the experimentally determined cisplatin IC50 in both H1299 and A549 cells. XDH and ITPA may represent candidate prognostic and functionally relevant purine metabolism-related genes in NSCLC. The integrated clinical, computational, and cellular findings support their association with NSCLC progression-related phenotypes, while the underlying molecular mechanisms and broader clinical applicability require further investigation.

title: Integrative Multi-Model Analysis Identifies a Core Gene Signature Associated with WEE1 Inhibitor Resistance, the Resistance-Associated Tumor Microenvironment, and Therapeutic Vulnerability in Ovarian Cancer.
abstract: Ovarian cancer is the most lethal gynecological malignancy, and acquired resistance to chemotherapy and targeted therapy is a central cause of treatment failure. The WEE1 inhibitor AZD1775 (adavosertib) has shown clinical activity in ovarian cancer, particularly in tumors with TP53 dysfunction, but acquired resistance frequently emerges, and its molecular basis remains incompletely understood. This study aims to identify a conserved, cross-species gene signature associated with the AZD1775-resistant state, to characterize its relationship with the Tumor Immune Microenvironment (TIME) and patient prognosis, and to nominate candidate drugs for combination testing. Transcriptomic data from a self-established murine AZD1775-resistance model (ID8 vs ID8R; RNA-seq, GSE313926) and from publicly available human AZD1775-resistant ovarian cancer cells (ES-2 vs ES-2R clones; GSE142124) were integrated. Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs) were intersected across models, Weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) was applied to the ID8/ID8R data, and a Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) network was used to prioritize connected candidates. In the TCGA Ovarian Cancer (TCGA-OV) cohort, ESTIMATE and five immune deconvolution algorithms (CIBERSORT, EPIC, TIMER, MCP-counter, and quanTIseq) were used to estimate stromal/immune admixture. The prognostic associations were assessed in Kaplan-Meier Plotter. Candidate drugs were prioritized from CellMiner using a pre-specified effect-size threshold, and drug combinations with AZD1775 were tested in ID8R cells by CCK-8 with Chou-Talalay analysis. A nine-gene signature (VCAN, RNASEL, PROS1, TNFRSF9, PXDN, KCNH1, KLF11, ATF3, and CDK15) was consistently upregulated across resistant models and within the resistance-associated WGCNA module. ESTIMATE and deconvolution analyses associated the signature with stromal/CAF and endothelial compartments, with weaker, method-dependent associations with immune-cell fractions. The nine-gene score was associated with overall survival, with heterogeneous direction for individual genes (VCAN, ATF3, CDK15, KLF11, and PXDN adverse; TNFRSF9, KCNH1, RNASEL protective). CellMiner drug sensitivity prediction and in vitro validation revealed that cell lines with high expression of the core gene set were more sensitive to Bleomycin, Lenvatinib, and Dasatinib; combinations with AZD1775 produced additive-to-synergistic effects under the standard Chou-Talalay grading (CI < 0.9) in ID8R. These agents are nominated as candidate combination partners for experimental testing. Cross-species integration of a murine isogenic resistance pair with independent human resistant clones identifies a nine-gene panel associated with the AZD1775-resistant state and with resistance-coupled stromal-myeloid remodeling, adverse prognosis and differential drug sensitivity in ovarian cancer. Because the panel was derived by association and several of its genes are predominantly expressed by stromal, myeloid, and activated immune cells rather than malignant cells, it should be regarded as a cross-compartment, resistance-associated marker rather than a set of causal drivers; functional perturbation and validation in independent resistant models are required. Nevertheless, the panel may help stratify patients for WEE1-inhibitor therapy and prioritize candidate combination partners for experimental testing. Cross-species integration nominates a nine-gene signature associated with the AZD1775-resistant state and resistance-coupled stromal-myeloid remodeling in ovarian cancer. The signature is a candidate marker of resistance-associated states and of drug response.
